Either is auto-continuable, but **next** is the better fit for an auto-continued slice given size + scope.

## Phase 7.x.reader.next — multi-chapter navigation (Prev / Next chapter)

Adds intra-Reader Prev / Next chapter affordances to the rework Reader. New `ListChaptersUseCase` (a thin projection over the existing `MangaDetailsRepository` — see §73.3 for why no new `ChaptersRepository`); new `ReaderState.chapters` field with three convenience properties (`currentChapterIndex`, `canGoPrev`, `canGoNext`); two new sealed `ReaderIntent` cases (`OnNextChapter`, `OnPrevChapter`); `ReaderViewModel` gains the 4th constructor dependency plus two reducer branches that route through the same `onEnter` pathway used by initial entry — in-place state mutation rather than pop+push nav (see §73.2 for why). `ReaderTopBar` gains two `IconButton`s ("‹" / "›") rendered between back and overflow. Closes the "no Next / Previous chapter within the Reader" gap that has stood since Phase 7.x.reader landed the single-chapter shell (§59).

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §73.1 — goal (single-chapter shell → multi-chapter navigation parity with legacy `goToNextChapter` / `goToPreviousChapter`)
- §73.2 — strategy: in-place state mutation (option B) vs pop+push (option A); picked B for legacy-parity, no new effect needed, chapter-list cached, no nav-flicker UX
- §73.3 — repository strategy: reuse `MangaDetailsRepository` (option B) vs new `ChaptersRepository` (option A); picked B because legacy's single endpoint returns both metadata + chapters in one `MangaInfo` payload — A would either duplicate the fetch or delegate (dead-weight interface)
- §73.4 — fire-and-forget `runFetch` with tracked `Job`: solves the concurrent-collector race that emerges once intra-manga Next / Prev can trigger `OnEnter` while a previous streaming page-flow (Prochan) is still alive. `MviViewModel.submit()` runs each intent in its own `viewModelScope.launch` — the OLD chapter's emissions would race the NEW chapter's `updateState` without job cancellation
- §73.5 — chapter-list failure is silent (no `ReaderEffect.ShowError` emit). Buttons disable via `canGoPrev` / `canGoNext`; surfacing the failure as a snackbar would mask successfully-rendered pages
- §73.6 — files (5 in foundation+VM commit, 1 in UI commit; two commits because of per-commit cap + clear seam between strict-MVI plumbing and the visible top-bar surface)
- §73.7 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 green across both commits)
- §73.8 — SOLID pointer
- §73.9 — deliberate deferrals (chapter-position label "23 / 156", hold-to-jump-N-chapters, currentPageIndex preservation on intra-chapter nav, pre-fetching the next chapter's pages, chapter-bookmark indicators on chevrons, per-source ordering toggle)

### Per-file SOLID checklist

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/reader/ListChaptersUseCase.kt`** (NEW)

1. **SRP**: ✓ One responsibility — projecting the chapter list out of a manga-details fetch and returning it as `AppResult<List<Chapter>>`. No fetch-orchestration, no caching, no chapter-sorting; the use case is a one-statement `when`-expression body.
2. **OCP**: ✓ The use case is itself a leaf — it doesn't host extension points but also doesn't constrain extension. Adding a future cache-first variant would be a sibling use case (`ObserveChaptersUseCase` with Flow shape), not a modification here.
3. **LSP**: ✓ No inheritance. Constructor takes the `MangaDetailsRepository` interface, not the data impl — any future replacement impl that honours the `fetchDetails(manga): AppResult<MangaDetails>` contract works without modification.
4. **ISP**: ✓ The use case's public surface is one `suspend operator fun invoke(manga: Manga): AppResult<List<Chapter>>` — the minimum possible. Consumer's call site (`listChapters(manga)`) is identical in shape to every other use case in the codebase, so the surface is also discoverable.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Constructor-injected `MangaDetailsRepository` (an interface from `:domain`), never the data impl. Bound by Koin in `composeApp`'s composition root (`readerReworkModule` resolves it from `detailsReworkModule`'s `single<MangaDetailsRepository>`). The use case lives entirely in `:domain` — no `:data`, no `:platform`, no `:presentation` reach.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain` only. Imports are `me.manga.kira.core.result.AppResult`, `me.manga.kira.domain.model.Chapter`, `me.manga.kira.domain.model.Manga`, `me.manga.kira.domain.repository.MangaDetailsRepository`. All `:core` + `:domain`; no upward reach.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`, no `Thread`. The `when` expression on `AppResult` is exhaustive — both `Success` and `Failure` handled. No nullable types in the public surface.
8. **Naming**: ✓ `ListChaptersUseCase` — verb-prefix matches the existing `FetchChapterPagesUseCase`, `ObserveReadingModeUseCase`, `SetReadingModeUseCase`, `FetchMangaDetailsUseCase` family. `invoke(manga: Manga)` parameter name matches every other manga-targeted use case in the project. Discoverable.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ 46-line KDoc covering: (a) phase context (Phase 7.x.reader.next foundation — Reader needs the chapter list for Next/Prev), (b) the "why thin use case over `MangaDetailsRepository` rather than `ChaptersRepository`" rationale with three explicit bullets (legacy single-endpoint design, dead-weight-interface argument, presentation-friendly projection), (c) cost-vs-caching analysis (refetches full `MangaDetails` per call, future-proofed cache-first switchpath), (d) error semantics (failures propagate via `AppResult.Failure`; empty list is a valid `Success`), (e) cancellation contract (propagates through repository call), (f) DIP rationale on constructor parameter.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable with a fake `MangaDetailsRepository` that returns `AppResult.Success(MangaDetails(...))` or `AppResult.Failure(...)`. Three test cases cover the full behaviour: (a) success → list extracted, (b) success with empty chapters → empty list, (c) failure → same failure propagated. No coroutine timing concerns — the use case is a single suspend call with no flow.

**`presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderState.kt`** (modified)

1. **SRP**: ✓ `ReaderState`'s job is "describe the immutable Reader screen state". Adding `chapters: List<Chapter>` plus three derived `get()`-only convenience props extends the same responsibility — the convenience props are pure projections of the state, not state in their own right (no `.copy()` argument). Same posture as the existing `hasPages` / `isInitialLoading` derived props.
2. **OCP**: ✓ The state is a `data class` with default-valued constructor params; adding a new param with a default value (`emptyList()`) is the canonical OCP-friendly extension — existing call sites that omit the field continue to compile and behave identically.
3. **LSP**: ✓ Implements the `MviState` marker interface; no contract widening.
4. **ISP**: ✓ The convenience props are split into three single-purpose getters rather than one `NavigationState` value class — consumers that only need `canGoNext` don't pay for the rest, and the names read like prose at the call site (`if (current.canGoNext)`).
5. **DIP**: ✓ Data-only — depends on `:domain` `Chapter`, `Manga`, `Page`, `ReadingMode` plus `:core` `AppError` and `:presentation/mvi` `MviState`. No upward reach.

The `chapter?.let { ... } ?: -1` pattern in `currentChapterIndex` uses safe-call elvis — no force-unwrap. `currentChapterIndex in 0..<chapters.lastIndex` is safe when `chapters.isEmpty()` (lastIndex is `-1`, range is empty, `in` returns false).

## Phase 7.x.reader.pageindicator — chapter-position label in top bar

Closes the §73.9 "Chapter-position label in the top bar" deferral. Pure presentation polish — one file, one new `Text`, no MVI surface change, no VM change. `ReaderTopBar` renders a 1-based "N / total" between the Prev and Next chevrons. Conditional on `chaptersCount > 0 && currentChapterIndex >= 0` — both fail during the initial chapter-list-fetch window and during the defensive chapter-not-in-list path, mirroring the §73-shipped `canGo*` disabled posture for the same window.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §74.1 — goal (surface "where I am in the chapter list" right next to the Next / Prev chevrons; legacy parity)
- §74.2 — layout: inline the `Text` between the chevrons (option B) vs wrap Prev + label + Next in a dedicated `Row` (option A); picked B because Material3's `TopAppBar.actions` is itself a `Row` with `Arrangement.End`, so inlining is the same shape with one less wrapper, and the standard 8.dp action-spacing matches the existing back ← / overflow ⋯ pattern
- §74.3 — visibility: conditional render (option B) vs always-visible with sentinel text (option A); picked B for consistency with the chevrons' disabled posture during the initial fetch window — the user sees the whole nav cluster fade in together
- §74.4 — files (1 — one file, one composable, one new `Text` plus two new params)
- §74.5 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 all green)
- §74.6 — SOLID pointer
- §74.7 — deliberate deferrals (per-page indicator HUD "page 7 / 24" total, chapter-title-in-label merge, tap-to-jump dialog)

## Phase 6.4.x.statistics — reading-session timer port

Closes the load-bearing "user's read-minutes total stops growing while they use the rework Reader" gap. Brings the legacy `ReaderViewModel.onScreenResume()` / `onScreenPause()` posture into the rework via two new screen-lifecycle intents (`OnScreenResumed` / `OnScreenPaused`), a new `:domain` repository interface (`ReadingSessionRepository`) with begin/end verbs, two pass-through use cases, a strangler-fig `:data` impl that delegates to the legacy `:shared` `StatisticsRepository` singleton (so both readers contribute to the same on-disk `READ_MINUTES` counter), and a `DisposableEffect(Unit)` in `ReaderScreenContent` that brackets the session.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §75.1 — goal (legacy `StatisticsRepository` is bound as `single` in `SharedModule.kt:238`; without the bracket the rework Reader doesn't contribute to the user-visible Statistics totals)
- §75.2 — strangler-fig delegate (option B) vs port-the-persistence-graph (option A); picked B because crossover correctness requires a single source of truth — the on-disk counter must not visibly drop at the Phase 9.x route-swap, and the layer-discipline pattern matches `ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl`'s reuse of `SourcesRepository`
- §75.3 — `DisposableEffect(Unit)` (option C) vs `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` (option A — no exit hook) vs `LaunchedEffect(manga, chapter)` (option B — double-bills intra-manga nav); picked C because `onDispose` is the only Compose primitive that always fires on tear-down, and `Unit` key keeps the session continuous across intra-manga Next / Prev (legacy parity with `ReaderActivity.onResume/onPause`)
- §75.4 — files (5 foundation + 4 VM-UI consumption across two source commits)
- §75.5 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 all green on both source commits)
- §75.6 — SOLID pointer (this section)
- §75.7 — deliberate deferrals (per-chapter session granularity, resume-on-last-page persistence, total-time HUD, read-streak tracking, long-idle-pause auto-stop)

Class-level KDoc covers SRP (one rule = "bracket a session"), the "begin/end" vs "trackSession(block)" decision (MVI atomicity + legacy posture preservation), cross-strangler-fig persistence (both readers feed `StorageKeys.READ_MINUTES`), the sequential-call idempotence contract (begin overwrites prior start, end no-ops on no-session, sub-minute sessions dropped), no-`AppResult` rationale, and DIP boundary.

### Per-file SOLID checklist

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/repository/ReadingSessionRepository.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ The interface declares two methods that together describe ONE rule — "bracket a reading session so the persistence layer can record elapsed minutes". Both methods are absolutely-minimum verbs (`begin()`, `suspend fun end()`); there is no "tick", "pause-and-resume", "elapsed", or "format-as-string" method, because none of those are part of the bracket. The minute-conversion math, the in-memory `sessionStartMillis` storage, and the sub-minute-drop policy all live in the impl. The interface does not even know that the unit of measurement is minutes (the `end()` return is `Unit`; the persistence sink is opaque to the contract). One responsibility, expressed minimally.
2. **OCP**: ✓ Adding a new bracket verb (e.g. `pause()` / `resume()`) would be an additive extension — existing consumers continue to use `begin` / `end` unchanged. Adding a new method `suspend fun observeElapsed(): Flow<Long>` would also be additive. The interface is positioned to grow without churn.
3. **LSP**: ✓ Any impl satisfying the two method signatures + their KDoc contracts (begin idempotent under multiple calls; end no-op on no-session; sub-minute dropped) is substitutable. The legacy delegate impl honours all three contracts because the legacy `StatisticsRepository` already does. A future in-memory test double would honour them by construction. No precondition tightening, no postcondition relaxation.
4. **ISP**: ✓ Two methods. Cannot be narrower without losing the bracket semantics. The consumer's two use cases each see exactly one method — `StartReadingSessionUseCase` sees `begin()`, `EndReadingSessionUseCase` sees `end()`. If a future consumer needed only one half of the bracket (e.g. a test double that only records starts), they could mock just that method; the interface doesn't force them to implement both ends of the bracket if they only care about one. (Kotlin's default behaviour requires implementing both, but the conceptual ISP property holds — neither method is dead weight.)
5. **DIP**: ✓ `:domain` interface, zero imports beyond `kotlin.coroutines` (implicit via `suspend`). The consumers (use cases, and through them the VM) depend on this abstraction; the impl in `:data` depends on the legacy `:shared` type, but that dependency is structural at the strangler-fig boundary (documented). Composition-root wiring (Koin) connects the interface to the impl.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain`. No `:data` reach, no `:platform` reach, no `:shared` reach, no `:presentation` reach. Pure abstraction.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`, no `Thread`. The `suspend` modifier on `end()` is the only Kotlin-coroutine reach, and it's a contract-level requirement (the impl writes to persistent storage).
8. **Naming**: ✓ `begin` / `end` is the bracket-pair vocabulary documented in the KDoc rationale. Symmetric, two-syllable, and (deliberately) not the legacy `startReadingSession` / `endReadingSession` names — the rework uses the shorter verbs because the type already says "session" and the noun-suffix would be redundant (parallels the rest of the rework's verb-only repository methods).
9. **KDoc**: ✓ 50-line class-level KDoc covers SRP, the "begin/end" vs "trackSession(block)" decision, the cross-strangler-fig persistence contract (both readers feed `StorageKeys.READ_MINUTES`), the three-point idempotence/safety contract (begin overwrites prior start, end safe on no-session, sub-minute dropped), the no-`AppResult` rationale (write-only side effect, no actionable failure surface), and DIP. Each method has a per-method KDoc documenting its specific contract (begin: "records `now()` in memory, no I/O, second begin overwrites"; end: "persists elapsed time, safe on no-session, sub-minute dropped").
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable through a fake impl: `class FakeSessionRepo : ReadingSessionRepository { var begins = 0; var ends = 0; override fun begin() { begins++ }; override suspend fun end() { ends++ } }`. The use cases that consume it become trivially testable: a single call to `StartReadingSessionUseCase().invoke()` should leave `fake.begins == 1`. The VM's two new reducer branches are similarly testable through the fake.

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/reader/StartReadingSessionUseCase.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ The class owns ONE rule — "delegate to `ReadingSessionRepository.begin`". No conditional, no transformation, no logging. Single-line `operator fun invoke()` body. This is the right amount of code for a use case whose entire job is to be a stable, testable seam between the VM and the repository — the alternative (have the VM call the repository directly) would couple the VM to a `:data`-bound type and lose the test seam.
2. **OCP**: ✓ The class is closed under modification (no inheritance hierarchy, no extension points). ### End-of-slice verdict

- Foundation change committed at `01a53d3` (5 files at the per-commit cap — 3 new domain + 1 new data + 1 modified composeApp). VM + UI consumption committed at `5ca1473` (4 files — 1 intent + 1 VM + 1 UI + 1 composeApp). Two commits because of the per-commit cap and because the seam between the bottom-up DI plumbing (foundation) and the top-down behaviour wiring (VM + UI) is a natural review boundary.
- Close-out (this SOLID entry + ARCHITECTURE.md §75) committed separately.
- Android compile gate: `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` green on both source commits.
- iOS compile gates: `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` + `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` green on both source commits.
- Desktop compile: not explicitly re-run; all symbols touched are `commonMain` (no Skia-specific or AWT-specific reach in either change).
- iOS framework linking + on-device "minute counter increments after 60s of reading" smoke test: Windows-impossible, deferred to user's Mac.
- Layer boundaries: no violations. `:domain` change is one new interface + two new use cases (all single-method classes). `:data` change is one new strangler-fig delegate (two-line method bodies + 40-line KDoc). `:presentation` change is two new sealed intent cases + 2 reducer branches + 2 constructor deps + 1 KDoc paragraph. `:composeApp` change is 3 new bindings + 1 viewModel-arg bump + 1 KDoc paragraph. `:ui` change is 1 new `import` + 1 `DisposableEffect(Unit)` block + 11 comment lines. No layer reaches into a layer below it that it didn't already reach into.
- Behaviour preservation: ✓ for current users — rework Reader still isn't user-facing (legacy chapter-images route untouched). For the rework Reader internally: every existing render path (loading, error, success, empty, Prev/Next, top-bar position label) is byte-identical to §74; the only added behaviour is the begin/end bracket around the screen's lifetime, which delegates to the same legacy persistence call the legacy Reader uses. For the user's lifetime-read-minutes counter (consumed by the Statistics screen, which is still legacy-routed): ✓ monotonic across the strangler-fig — the rework Reader now contributes to the same on-disk cell as the legacy Reader.
- MVI contract: extended (additively, OCP-correctly). Sealed-interface extension on `ReaderIntent` is caught by exhaustive-`when` in the reducer — proves the OCP guard works as intended. No `ReaderState` extension (write-only counter has no UI consumer). No `ReaderEffect` extension (no nav, no snackbar).
- Strangler-fig integrity: ✓ the `:data` impl is the only new touch-point with `:shared`; the boundary is documented in the impl's KDoc + the Koin module's `Cross-module dependencies` block. Phase 9.x route-swap can retire the legacy `StatisticsRepository.startReadingSession` / `endReadingSession` methods (and possibly the whole legacy class) without touching `:domain` or `:presentation` or `:ui`.
- Load-bearing fixes preserved: `maxBitmapSize(Undefined, Undefined)`, `ContentScale.Fit` for pagers, `ContentScale.FillWidth` for the LazyColumn, `.zoomable(rememberZoomState())` on every layout (§67), `.background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)` on the LazyColumn (§68), `initialPageIndex` threaded for mode-toggle scroll-position preservation (§69), `screenHeightDb` threaded for reserved-height placeholders (§70), `val errorPainter = painter` receiver-shadowing workaround for the in-error Retry button (§71), `onOpenInWebView` closure-threading for Open-in-WebView routing (§72), fire-and-forget `runFetch` + `runListChapters` with tracked `Job?` from §73, chapter-position label conditional render from §74. None touched.
- Deliberate deferrals captured in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §75.7 (per-chapter session granularity, resume-on-last-page persistence, total-time HUD, read-streak/daily-target tracking, long-idle-pause auto-stop).

Single commit, no plan needed.

## Phase 7.x.reader.resumeposition — per-chapter last-read-page persistence

Lands a UX the legacy reader never delivered: when the user closes the rework Reader mid-chapter, the page they were on is restored on re-entry. Brings a new `:domain` `ReadProgressRepository` interface (`suspend save(chapterUrl, pageIndex)` + `suspend load(chapterUrl): Int?`), two pass-through use cases (`SavePagePositionUseCase` / `LoadPagePositionUseCase`), an `ObservableSettings`-backed `:data` impl with a hash-key + stored-URL collision guard (Desktop's `java.util.prefs.Preferences.MAX_KEY_LENGTH = 80` forces the hashing), three new Koin bindings, and a VM consumption pass that seeds `state.currentPageIndex` in `onEnter` and fire-and-forgets a save in `onPageChanged`. Net-new persistence, not strangler-fig — the legacy `HistoryItemD.lastReadPage` column is dead-write (always set to 0 by `historyViewModel.updateHistoryItem`), so there is no existing on-disk state to preserve.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §76.1 — goal (legacy reader never delivered this UX; today rework always opens at page 0)
- §76.2 — net-new ObservableSettings cell (option B) vs strangler-fig over legacy Room column (option A); picked B because the legacy column is dead-write (no value loss at the Phase 9.x route swap), layer cleanliness (no `:shared` Room reach), per-chapter granularity falls out for free, and the storage shape mirrors the established Phase 6.4.x.mode template
- §76.3 — hash-key + stored-URL collision guard (`"reader.last_page." + chapter.url.hashCode().toUInt().toString(36)` for the ≤24-char key; value `"${chapterUrl}|${pageIndex}"` with split-on-`|` + URL-match verification on load); the naive `putInt(longKey, _)` shape would throw on Desktop's `java.util.prefs.Preferences` 80-char key limit
- §76.4 — VM consumption (suspend cascade through `onEnter` → atomic state landing; fire-and-forget save on `onPageChanged` with captured `chapterUrl` so fast Next/Prev still writes against the right chapter; deliberate decision NOT to launch a separate coroutine for the load — preserves the atomic-state-update contract)
- §76.5 — bounds clamping (the saved page may be past the new chapter's last-index if the chapter shrank on re-publish; handled by the existing `runFetch` Success branch's `coerceIn(0, pages.lastIndex)` — no extra check in the use case or repo)
- §76.6 — files (5 foundation + 2 VM consumption across two source commits)
- §76.7 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 all green on both source commits)
- §76.8 — SOLID pointer (this section)
- §76.9 — deliberate deferrals (no UI to clear saved positions, no incognito-mode parity, no stale-entry cleanup, no streaming Flow shape, no telemetry of resume events)

- `data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/ReadProgressRepositoryImpl.kt` (new) — Backed by `ObservableSettings`. ~80-line class KDoc covers the Desktop 80-char key-length constraint, the hash-key derivation (`hashCode().toUInt().toString(36)` for a ≤7-char alphanumeric suffix + 17-char prefix = ≤24 chars), the collision-safety contract (value stored as `"${chapterUrl}|${pageIndex}"`; on load, split, verify URL matches, return null on mismatch — converts wrong-page bug into "start at page 0" graceful fallback), the separator choice (`|` is not a valid URL char per RFC 3986), why no `flowOn(io)` (multiplatform-settings impls wrap in-memory state — pinning would add a context-switch hop with no benefit; same posture as `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl`), why `suspend` despite non-blocking writes (contract parity + door open for future I/O-bound backend), no-op write protection (`ObservableSettings.putString` short-circuits identical writes + VM `onPageChanged` already guards on `clamped == current.currentPageIndex`), lifecycle (`single` — backing settings is itself a singleton, impl holds no per-call state), and thread-safety.

### Per-file SOLID checklist

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/repository/ReadProgressRepository.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ The interface declares two methods that together describe ONE rule — "persist one chapter's last-viewed page index, retrieve it on demand". No "observe all positions" Flow, no "clear all", no "list all chapters with saved positions", no "is-chapter-resumable" predicate. The hash-key derivation, the collision-safety guard, the on-disk encoding, and the no-op-write short-circuit all live in the impl — the interface does not even know that the storage backend is `ObservableSettings` (the contract's chapter-identity is `chapterUrl: String` and the value is a non-negative `Int`; everything else is impl detail). One responsibility, expressed at the absolute minimum verbal surface.
2. **OCP**: ✓ Additive extensions (e.g. `suspend fun observe(chapterUrl): Flow<Int?>`, `suspend fun clearAll()`, `suspend fun listSavedChapters(): List<String>`) would be net-new methods leaving existing methods unchanged. The interface is positioned to grow without churn. The two-method shape is the minimum closed-under-modification surface for the current Reader's resume-position UX.
3. **LSP**: ✓ Any impl satisfying the two method signatures + the KDoc contracts (load returns null on absent OR on hash collision; save is idempotent under repeated `(chapterUrl, pageIndex)`; concurrent calls don't tear writes) is substitutable. The `ObservableSettings`-backed impl honours all three by construction. A future in-memory test double or a future Room-backed impl would honour them by construction.
4. **ISP**: ✓ Two methods. Cannot be narrower without losing the round-trip persistence semantics. Each use case sees exactly one method — `SavePagePositionUseCase` sees `save`, `LoadPagePositionUseCase` sees `load`. If a future write-only consumer or read-only consumer arrived, neither method is dead weight. (Kotlin's default behaviour forces an impl to implement both methods, but the conceptual ISP property holds — every method is consumed by at least one use case.)
5. **DIP**: ✓ `:domain` interface, zero imports beyond `kotlin.coroutines` (implicit via `suspend`). The consumers (use cases, and through them the VM) depend on this abstraction; the impl in `:data` depends on `ObservableSettings` (multiplatform-settings, bound by `PlatformModule.<target>.kt`), but the consumer-impl coupling is mediated through Koin's composition root.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain`. No `:data` reach, no `:platform` reach, no `:shared` reach, no `:presentation` reach. Pure abstraction.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`, no `Thread`. The `suspend` modifier is the only coroutine reach, and it's a contract-level requirement (door open for a future I/O-bound backend even if the current impl is in-memory).
8. **Naming**: ✓ `ReadProgressRepository` matches the `XxxRepository` convention used by every other `:domain` repository (`ChapterPagesRepository`, `ReadingModeRepository`, `MangaDetailsRepository`, `LibraryRepository`, `SourcesRepository`, `ReadingSessionRepository`). `save` / `load` are symmetric two-verb names; deliberately not `persist` / `retrieve` (more syllables, same meaning) or `setPage` / `getPage` (would imply nullable `getPage`-returning-`Int` with no way to express absence). The parameter names `chapterUrl: String` and `pageIndex: Int` name the contract precisely (URL is the identity; index is the position).
9. **KDoc**: ✓ ~80-line class-level KDoc covers SRP (one rule = "persist one chapter's last-viewed page index"), the net-new persistence boundary (legacy column dead-write — documented with a pointer to where the legacy reader passes 0 verbatim), chapter-identity semantics (`chapterUrl` is the legacy primary-key surrogate; reused by the Reader's intent payloads), the collision-safety contract (impl MAY hash but MUST return null on collision — this is the load-bearing constraint that makes the `:data` impl's stored-URL guard the right design), the no-`AppResult` rationale (matches `ReadingSessionRepository.end` and `ReadingModeRepository.set`), idempotence (repeated identical saves no-op at the backend), and DIP. Per-method KDocs document the load's null-for-absent-OR-collision semantics and the save's idempotence contract explicitly.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable through a fake impl: `class FakeReadProgressRepo : ReadProgressRepository { val saves = mutableMapOf<String, Int>(); override suspend fun save(url: String, page: Int) { saves[url] = page }; override suspend fun load(url: String): Int? = saves[url] }`. Each use case is then trivially testable against the fake. The VM's `onEnter` seed and `onPageChanged` write are also testable through the fake (assert the saved value matches the dispatched `OnPageChanged`'s clamped index).

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/reader/SavePagePositionUseCase.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ Owns ONE rule — "delegate to `ReadProgressRepository.save`". Single-line `suspend operator fun invoke(chapterUrl: String, pageIndex: Int)` body. No conditional, no transformation, no logging. The clamping policy (page must be in `0..pages.lastIndex`) lives in the VM's `onPageChanged`; the idempotence policy lives in the repository; the use case is a stable, testable seam.
2. **OCP**: ✓ Closed under modification (no inheritance hierarchy, no extension points). Open under extension via the use-case Decorator pattern — a future `LoggedSavePagePositionUseCase(delegate)` could wrap it without modifying this class.
3. **LSP**: ✓ N/A (not in an inheritance hierarchy).
4. **ISP**: ✓ One method, two scalar parameters. `operator fun invoke(chapterUrl, pageIndex)` is the absolute-minimum callable surface — any narrower would lose the round-trip information needed to identify the persistence key.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Depends on `ReadProgressRepository` (the `:domain` abstraction), not on the impl. Construction is via Koin's `factory { SavePagePositionUseCase(get()) }` — the `get()` resolves the singleton impl bound by `ReaderReworkModule`.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain`. No `:data` reach, no `:platform` reach.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`, no `Thread`. The class body is a single-line delegation.
8. **Naming**: ✓ `SavePagePositionUseCase` matches the established `XxxYyyUseCase` convention. The verb-noun shape (`SavePagePosition`) reads as the action it performs. `operator fun invoke()` matches the rest of the rework's use cases.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ ~25-line class-level KDoc covers Phase context, SRP (single-line delegate to the repository), the two-use-case vs one-tracker decision (mirrors Phase 6.4.x.mode `Observe/SetReadingModeUseCase` and Phase 6.4.x.statistics `Start/EndReadingSessionUseCase` — symmetric independent test seams beat a two-method "Tracker" class), `suspend` shape (matches repository's suspend contract; the VM's call site is already inside a suspending lambda — `viewModelScope.launch { savePagePosition(...) }`), idempotence note (repeated identical saves no-op at the backend), and DIP-Koin-factory rationale.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable: `val fake = FakeReadProgressRepo(); SavePagePositionUseCase(fake).invoke("url", 5); assertEquals(5, fake.saves["url"])`. The use case being a separate class (rather than a method on the repository) is what makes this seam exist at all — testing the VM's `onPageChanged` reducer's save side effect requires a `SavePagePositionUseCase` test double, not a full repository test double.

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/reader/LoadPagePositionUseCase.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ Owns ONE rule — "delegate to `ReadProgressRepository.load`". Single-line `suspend operator fun invoke(chapterUrl: String): Int?` body. The "use the saved page if any, otherwise start at 0" fallback lives in the VM's `onEnter` (`loadPagePosition(chapter.url) ?: 0`) where the policy belongs; this use case is a pure read-through.
2. **OCP**: ✓ Closed under modification, open under Decorator-style extension.
3. **LSP**: ✓ N/A.
4. **ISP**: ✓ One method, one scalar parameter.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Depends on `:domain` abstraction.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain`.
7. **No banned features**: ✓.
8. **Naming**: ✓ Symmetric with `SavePagePositionUseCase` (`Load…` is the canonical antonym verb for `Save…`). `suspend operator fun invoke()` is the established convention.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ ~25-line class-level KDoc covers Phase context, SRP (single-line delegate), the null-for-absent-OR-collision semantics (the VM treats both cases identically — the distinction matters at the contract level but not the policy level), the phase invariant that the saved page may be past the new chapter's last-index after a chapter shrinks on re-publish (handled by the VM's existing `runFetch` coerceIn — explicit cross-reference), why no bounds check at the use-case level (policy lives in the VM reducer where the page list is available — keeps the use case a pure pass-through), and DIP.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable: `val fake = FakeReadProgressRepo(); assertNull(LoadPagePositionUseCase(fake).invoke("never-saved")); fake.saves["url"] = 5; assertEquals(5, LoadPagePositionUseCase(fake).invoke("url"))`.

**`data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/ReadProgressRepositoryImpl.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ Owns ONE rule — "translate between the on-disk encoded representation of a `(chapterUrl, pageIndex)` pair and the typed surface that `ReadProgressRepository` declares, with a collision-safety guard for the hash-based storage key derivation". Three private constants (`KEY_PREFIX`, `SEPARATOR`, the `keyFor` derivation), two public methods, no instance state beyond the injected `settings`. The minute conversion, the `sessionStartMillis` field, the cross-strangler-fig delegation — none of those concerns from the statistics slice live here; this impl is a self-contained translator between the wire format and the domain types.
2. **OCP**: ✓ The two-method shape is closed under modification (changes to the wire format are bounded inside the impl — the public surface is the abstract `save`/`load` from the interface). Open under Koin substitution — a future Room-backed impl or in-memory impl could replace this binding without touching the use cases or the VM. The future-proofing comment in the class KDoc explicitly documents the path for extending the wire format (version-suffixed key prefix).
3. **LSP**: ✓ Implements `ReadProgressRepository` honouring all three KDoc contracts (load returns null on absent OR on hash collision via the stored-URL guard; save is idempotent under repeated identical writes via `ObservableSettings.putString`'s short-circuit; the `suspend` shape is honoured even though the underlying `ObservableSettings` writes are synchronous on every target).
4. **ISP**: ✓ The `ObservableSettings` interface exposes many methods (`getStringOrNull`, `putString`, `getIntOrNull`, `putInt`, `getBoolean`, `addListener`, `clear`, `remove`, …); this impl reaches exactly two — `getStringOrNull` and `putString`. The unused methods stay unused; the persistence surface is the minimum.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Depends on `ObservableSettings` (multiplatform-settings library type, bound as a `single` by `PlatformModule.<target>.kt` via `SettingsFactory.createObservable("yami_settings")`). This is the same singleton the Phase 6.4.x.mode `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl` consumes — by design, not coincidence. The constructor takes `settings: ObservableSettings`, never reaches into Koin's `get()` directly, never imports a Settings impl class (no `PreferencesSettings`, `AppleSettings`, `SharedPreferencesSettings` here). Composition-root wiring (Koin) connects the impl to the singleton.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:data/commonMain`. No `:platform` reach (the multiplatform-settings library lives in `core/commonMain` deps + the `:platform` `expect/actual` for the factory); no `:presentation`, no `:ui`, no `:shared` reach. The strangler-fig boundary that exists in `ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl` (reach into `:shared` `SourcesRepository`) and `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (reach into `:shared` `StatisticsRepository`) is deliberately ABSENT here — this is net-new persistence, not delegate-to-legacy.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`, no `Thread`. The two-method body is straightforward String manipulation + ObservableSettings calls. `lastIndexOf` returns `Int` (sentinel `-1`, handled by the `separatorAt <= 0 || separatorAt == raw.lastIndex` guard); `substring` returns `String`; `toIntOrNull` returns `Int?` (handled by the `takeIf { it >= 0 }` non-negative guard).
8. **Naming**: ✓ `ReadProgressRepositoryImpl` matches the `XxxRepositoryImpl` convention. `keyFor(chapterUrl: String): String` reads as the action it performs ("the key for this chapter URL"). Constants `KEY_PREFIX` and `SEPARATOR` are explicit about role rather than value (`KEY_PREFIX` not `READER_KEY`; `SEPARATOR` not `PIPE_CHAR`). Local variables (`encoded`, `raw`, `separatorAt`, `storedUrl`, `pageText`) each name the step they represent in the round trip.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ ~80-line class-level KDoc covers SRP, DIP, the Desktop 80-char `Preferences.MAX_KEY_LENGTH` constraint that forced the hash-key design, the hash-key derivation (`hashCode().toUInt().toString(36)` → ≤7 alphanumeric chars), the collision-safety contract (`String.hashCode` is not injective; stored-URL match is the load-bearing guard), the wire format on disk (`"${chapterUrl}|${pageIndex}"`), separator choice rationale (`|` is not a valid RFC 3986 URL char; sources URL-encode it as `%7C`), defensive parse-failure handling (negative or non-numeric values trigger null return), the future-proofing path (version-suffixed key prefix), the no-`AppResult` rationale (parity with Phase 6.4.x.mode), why no `flowOn(io)` (multiplatform-settings impls wrap in-memory state), the `suspend` shape rationale (door open for future I/O-bound backend), no-op write protection (`ObservableSettings.putString` short-circuits + VM `onPageChanged` already guards), lifecycle (`single` — backing settings is a singleton, impl holds no per-call state), and thread-safety. No per-method KDoc on the trivial method bodies (the class KDoc covers the contract; the methods are 1-7 lines each).
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable via a fake `ObservableSettings` (multiplatform-settings provides `MapSettings` for exactly this purpose). Test cases: (a) `save("url-A", 5)` then `load("url-A")` returns 5; (b) `load("never-saved")` returns null; (c) hash-collision test — manually inject a value `"different-url|5"` under the key derived from `"my-url"`'s hash, assert `load("my-url")` returns null (stored-URL mismatch guard fires); (d) malformed value test — manually inject `"no-separator"` under a known key, assert `load(...)` returns null (defensive parse-failure); (e) negative-page-index test — inject `"url|-5"`, assert null (the `>= 0` guard fires); (f) round-trip with a chapter URL that exceeds 80 chars to confirm Desktop's `Preferences` doesn't throw.

**`presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderViewModel.kt`** (modified)

1. **SRP**: ✓ The VM still has one responsibility — orchestrating Reader presentation state and routing user/lifecycle intents to the right `:domain` collaborator. The two new dependencies don't add a new responsibility; they extend the existing seed-and-persist responsibility to the page-position dimension. The `onEnter` seed-then-fetch sequence is a single coherent state transition (atomic `updateState` with all fields including the resume seed). The `onPageChanged` fire-and-forget save is a side effect that runs AFTER the synchronous reducer mutation — no policy logic in the launch lambda, just a pass-through to the use case. The VM remains a use-case dispatcher with zero domain logic.
2. **OCP**: ✓ No new branches in the exhaustive `when (intent)` block — the resume-position pair piggybacks on the existing `OnEnter` and `OnPageChanged` intents (the load happens in `onEnter`, the save happens in `onPageChanged`). This is a deliberate OCP win: persistence behaviour was extended without adding new intent surface (the alternative — an `OnLoadSavedPage` intent dispatched from the UI — would have widened the public surface for no observable benefit; the load is internal to the VM's `onEnter` flow). Two new constructor deps — additive, not a contract widening.
3. **LSP**: ✓ Extends `MviViewModel<ReaderState, ReaderIntent, ReaderEffect>` — no contract changes. The `onEnter` change from non-suspend to `suspend` is internal; the public `submit(intent: ReaderIntent)` surface remains identical (calls `handle(intent)` which was already suspend). The transitively-suspending `onNextChapter` / `onPrevChapter` are private and called only from `handle` — no caller surface change.
4. **ISP**: ✓ The VM's public surface is unchanged (`state: StateFlow<ReaderState>`, `effect: Flow<ReaderEffect>`, `submit(intent: ReaderIntent)` inherited from `MviViewModel`). Constructor gained two new dependencies (`LoadPagePositionUseCase`, `SavePagePositionUseCase`) — a refinement, not a contract widening (Koin handles the wiring; consumers never construct the VM directly). Each dep is single-method, used in exactly one reducer flow — minimum surface.
5. **DIP**: ✓ The two new dependencies are `:domain` use case classes (concrete classes, but injected as immutable singletons through Koin — substitutable for any impl honouring the `invoke()` / `suspend invoke()` contracts). No `:data` reach. No `ObservableSettings` reach — the VM delegates to the use cases, which delegate to the `:domain` interface, which Koin binds to the `:data` impl. Four-layer DIP chain, no shortcuts.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:presentation/commonMain`. No `:ui` reach, no `:data` reach, no `:platform` reach, no `:shared` reach.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`. The two new fields are non-nullable `val`s assigned via constructor injection. The `val chapterUrl = current.chapter?.url ?: return` pattern in `onPageChanged` uses safe-call + Elvis (no `!!`); the `loadPagePosition(chapter.url) ?: 0` pattern in `onEnter` uses Elvis on the use case's nullable return. The transitive suspend cascade through `onEnter` / `onNextChapter` / `onPrevChapter` is honoured at the language level (the compiler enforces it).
8. **Naming**: ✓ Constructor parameters `loadPagePosition` / `savePagePosition` are noun-phrases matching the established convention (`fetchPages`, `observeReadingMode`, `setReadingMode`, `listChapters`, `startReadingSession`, `endReadingSession` — all noun-phrases or verb-phrases naming what the dep does). The local variables `savedPage` (in `onEnter`) and `chapterUrl` (in `onPageChanged`) name the values they hold precisely. The single-line use-case call sites read as English (`loadPagePosition(chapter.url) ?: 0`, `savePagePosition(chapterUrl, clamped)`).

## Phase 7.x.reader.pagecounthud — page X/Y label in top bar

Pairs the §74 chapter-position label (between Prev / Next chevrons) with a new page-position label (after the Next chevron), so the user scanning the top bar sees both progress dimensions at once: `‹  chapter N / M  ›  page X / Y  ⋯`. Single-file `:ui` change: two new `ReaderTopBar` parameters (`currentPageIndex: Int`, `pagesCount: Int`), three new lines at the call site, one new conditional `Text` in the actions block, a 12-line inline comment documenting the parallel with §74 and the deliberate retention of the bottom HUD pill. No new MVI surface, no new use case, no new `:domain` types.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §77.1 — goal (parallel the §74 chapter-position label with a page-position label so chrome shows both dimensions at once)
- §77.2 — additive companion (option B) vs move-from-bottom-HUD (option A); picked B because removing the bottom HUD pill (which has shown page X/Y since Phase 7.x.reader.chrome) would be Rule 8(b) "refactor would change observable behavior" — block-and-ask. Adding a top-bar companion is purely additive. Surface complementarity: bottom HUD is near the gesture surface, top-bar label is near the chapter affordances.
- §77.3 — positional grouping (`‹  chapter N / M  ›  page X / Y  ⋯` — chapter affordances cluster around the chevrons, page-count follows as a separate group, then overflow; alternative of putting page-count between chevrons rejected for clarity)
- §77.4 — files (1 file in 1 source commit)
- §77.5 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 all green)
- §77.6 — SOLID pointer (this section)
- §77.7 — deliberate deferrals (no HUD vs top-bar mode picker, no page-scrubber slider, no icon for kebab overflow)

Three new lines in the `ReaderTopBar(...)` call site inside `ReaderScreenContent`: `currentPageIndex = state.currentPageIndex`, `pagesCount = state.pages.size`. New conditional `Text(...)` block in the actions section, positioned AFTER the Next-chapter `IconButton` and BEFORE the overflow-menu `IconButton`, gated on `pagesCount > 0` (mirrors the `chaptersCount > 0 && currentChapterIndex >= 0` gate for the chapter-position label, modulo that the page-position label has no analogue to "current chapter index can be -1 if chapter not found in list" — `currentPageIndex` is always in `0..pages.lastIndex` after the VM's onPageChanged clamp, so the simpler `pagesCount > 0` suffices). 12-line inline comment block above the new `Text` documents the parallel with §74, the gate semantics, the 1-based display rationale (matches the legacy "X / Y" pill and the bottom HUD), the deliberate retention of the bottom HUD pill (would have been Rule 8(b) to remove), and the shared `state.isUiVisible` fade semantics.

## Phase 7.x.reader.pagescrubber — horizontal slider for jump-to-page

Closes the deferral §77.7 floated in the prior slice: a horizontal `Slider` below the bottom HUD pill, gated on the same `state.isUiVisible` chrome fade, that lets the user drag to jump to any page in the current chapter — fully wired (drag actually moves the layout, not just a read-only progress indicator). Single-file `:ui` change. Re-uses `ReaderIntent.OnPageChanged(Int)` — no new MVI surface, no new use case, no `:domain` type, no `:platform` facade, no `:data` reach. Internal layout-side refactor: `initialPageIndex` → `currentPageIndex` rename across `ReaderPageLayout` + three child layouts, each getting a new `LaunchedEffect(currentPageIndex)` that calls `scrollToItem` / `scrollToPage` behind an if-guard to close the scrubber-drive loop.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §78.1 — goal (real jump-to-page affordance, not a read-only progress indicator; lives inside the same `isUiVisible` chrome gate as the bottom HUD).
- §78.2 — MVI re-use (re-dispatches the same `OnPageChanged(Int)` that organic scroll's snapshotFlow already emits; from the VM's view scrubber drag is indistinguishable from scrolling). Mirrors the §70 `OnRetry` re-use and §75 `OnPageChanged` re-use patterns.
- §78.3 — closing the layout loop (new `LaunchedEffect(currentPageIndex)` in each layout reacts to non-scroll updates to `currentPageIndex` and calls `scrollToItem` / `scrollToPage` only when the layout's own state lags; the if-guard makes scroll-driven updates a no-op, keeping the loop stable). Side-benefit: future deeplink-to-page / resume-on-specific-page slices reuse the same plumbing for free.
- §78.4 — `initialPageIndex` → `currentPageIndex` rename rationale (the parameter is no longer purely "initial" once it drives live scroll, so the name had become misleading; renamed across signature + call site + three child layouts; KDoc updated to document the dual role: initial-state for the remember*State + drive scroll-on-change).
- §78.5 — Slider config (value bound directly to `currentPageIndex.toFloat()` with a `coerceIn` guard for chapter-swap windows; `steps = pagesCount - 2` for snap-to-integer behavior since Material3 counts steps BETWEEN endpoints; `onValueChange` toInt-rounds and short-circuits identical indices before dispatching).
- §78.6 — bottom-overlay refactor (single `AnimatedVisibility` wrapping a `Column` that holds HUD + scrubber; HUD renders first (visually upper), scrubber renders second (visually lower for one-handed thumb reach); the HUD's existing `padding(bottom = spacing.lg)` provides natural separation; scrubber's own horizontal+vertical padding keeps it off the side edges).
- §78.7 — files (1 file in 1 source commit).
- §78.8 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 all green).
- §78.9 — SOLID pointer (this section).
- §78.10 — deliberate deferrals (no tick-density polish for long chapters, no continuous-stride `steps=0` variant, no animated scroll on scrubber-drive, no bookmark/chapter-resume callers wired to the new LaunchedEffect — all out of scope for the functional-correctness ship).

New private `ReaderPageScrubber` composable (binds Slider to `currentPageIndex.toFloat()`, computes `steps = pagesCount - 2`, dispatches `onPageChanged` from `onValueChange` only when the integer changed; padded horizontal=`spacing.lg`, vertical=`spacing.sm`). Bottom-center overlay refactored from a single HUD `AnimatedVisibility` into a single `AnimatedVisibility` wrapping a `Column` that contains the HUD pill (when `pageIndicator(state) != null`) followed by the scrubber (when `state.pages.size > 1`); outer gate composes both render conditions. ## Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageprogress — Coil download-% indicator on loading placeholder

Closes the deferral §78.10 floated in the prior slice: surfaces Coil's per-page download progress as a determinate circular indicator on the reader's loading placeholder. Multi-commit, plan-mode-scoped (`PLAN_pageprogress.md`) because the slice spans four layers (`:domain` → `:data` → `:presentation` → `:ui`), needs a new Android-only OkHttp interceptor wired into the existing `PlatformNetworkFetcher` expect/actual without disturbing load-bearing image-quality fixes, and lifts the previously-deferred Android RGB_565 + allowHardware(false) decoder hints from `:composeApp` into `:ui/reader/internal/` via a new internal expect/actual.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §79.1 — goal (determinate indicator on loading placeholder; three surfaces: `:domain` typed progress, `:data` MutableStateFlow<Map<...>> repo, `:ui` per-request listener).
- §79.2 — `:domain` types (sealed interface `PageDownloadProgress` with six variants: `Idle`, `Started`, `Fetching(Float)`, `Decoding`, `Loaded`, `Failed`; `PageProgressRepository` interface with `observe(pageUrl): Flow<PageDownloadProgress>` + `report(pageUrl, progress)`).
- §79.3 — `:data` impl (`MutableStateFlow<Map<String, PageDownloadProgress>>` + `.update { it + (key to value) }` for atomic per-key updates; `observe` returns `state.map { it[pageUrl] ?: Idle }.distinctUntilChanged()`).
- §79.4 — VM extension (`pageProgress: Map<String, PageDownloadProgress>` field added to `ReaderState`; `startObservingProgress(pageUrl)` collects from repo into state; tracked `Job?` per page url for cancel-on-leave; constructor arg bump 8 → 9 in `ReaderReworkModule.kt`).
- §79.5 — `:ui` listener + placeholder (per-request `.listener(onStart, onCancel, onSuccess, onError)` bridges Coil lifecycle events into `PageProgressRepository.report(...)`; `rememberUpdatedState` to keep the `remember`-cached `ImageRequest` invoking the latest progress callback after recompositions; the loading placeholder switches between determinate `CircularProgressIndicator(progress = fraction)` and indeterminate spinner based on the observed `PageDownloadProgress` variant).
- §79.6 — Android OkHttp byte interceptor (`OkHttpProgressInterceptor` wraps `Response.body` in a `ProgressResponseBody` that counts bytes via `okio.ForwardingSource`; reports `Fetching(fraction)` every 50ms + 1% change via Int tenThousandths comparison; `OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(...).build()` passed as `OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory(callFactory = { client })`; `GlobalContext.get()` for non-Compose Koin resolution at composition-root time; block-and-ask trigger #1 audited NOT met (Coil 3.4.0 default OkHttpClient is vanilla)).
- §79.7 — Reader decoder-hint lift (resolves the previously-documented deferral in `ReaderScreen.kt` — the rework Reader's inline `ImageRequest.Builder` did not call any analog of legacy `applyPlatformDecoderHints`; new `:ui/reader/internal/ReaderDecoderHints.{kt,android.kt,desktop.kt,ios.kt}` expect/actual with Android RGB_565 + allowHardware(false) actual, iOS / Desktop no-op actuals).
- §79.8 — files (8 source commits enumerated, all ≤5 files per commit).
- §79.9 — build gates (Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 all SUCCESSFUL across every source commit).
- §79.10 — SOLID pointer (this section).
- §79.11 — deliberate deferrals (iOS / Desktop per-byte ktor3 follow-on; no time-remaining smoothing; no per-page failed-state user message; no `Decoding` emission in this slice; no `PageProgressReporterAttacher` expect/actual facade — landed instead on per-request listener + Android-only interceptor).

### Files

### Per-file SOLID checklist

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/model/reader/PageDownloadProgress.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ One responsibility — name the lifecycle states a single page transitions through during decoding. Sealed interface with six variants (`Idle`, `Started`, `Fetching(Float)`, `Decoding`, `Loaded`, `Failed`) — no behaviour, just typed states. The smoothing/throttle logic lives in the Android interceptor (Phase 7.x close-out §79.6); the determinate-vs-indeterminate UI policy lives in `:ui/ReaderScreen.kt`; the per-page Flow plumbing lives in `:data/PageProgressRepositoryImpl.kt`. This file is the contract those collaborators agree on.
2. **OCP**: ✓ Sealed interface bounds the variant universe; new states (e.g., `Queued`, `Retrying(attempt: Int)`) extend the hierarchy without modifying existing variants. The exhaustive `when` at the `:ui` placeholder consumer fires compile errors on new variants — OCP-friendly closure.
3. **LSP**: ✓ Each variant is a `data class` or `object` with no method override; subtypes are fully interchangeable behind the sealed-interface reference. The `Fetching(fraction: Float)` data class's `fraction` is documented as `0f..1f` in its KDoc — the contract is honoured by every emitter (the interceptor's `coerceIn(0f, 1f)` + the `Started` initial state's `fraction = 0f` posture).
4. **ISP**: ✓ The variants expose only the data they need (`Fetching` has `fraction: Float`; `Failed` has `throwable: Throwable?`; the four nullary states are `object`s). No "kitchen sink" variant carrying a superset of fields.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Pure `:domain` types; depend only on Kotlin stdlib (`Float`, `Throwable`). No `:data`, `:platform`, `:presentation`, `:ui`, or `:shared` reach.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain`.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`. `Failed`'s `throwable` is nullable `Throwable?` — modelled, not asserted.
8. **Naming**: ✓ Variant names match Coil's lifecycle conceptually (`onStart` → `Started`, `onCancel` left implicit, `onSuccess` → `Loaded`, `onError` → `Failed`); the `Decoding` variant exists for future emission paths even though no surface emits it today (documented in `:domain` so a future decoder-stage slice can use it). `fraction` (not `progress`) avoids ambiguity with the variant's "progress" container nature.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ Sealed-interface class-level KDoc covers the lifecycle order, the `fraction` range invariant, the deliberate `Decoding` no-emitter status (documented as future-proofing), and the cross-reference to the `:data` repo and the `:ui` placeholder.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Trivially testable (pure ADT — `assertEquals(Fetching(0.5f), Fetching(0.5f))` etc.); no test required beyond the use-site coverage.

**`domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/repository/reader/PageProgressRepository.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ One responsibility — declare the `:domain`-side contract for "observe per-page progress" and "report per-page progress". Two methods, both single-purpose: `observe(pageUrl: String): Flow<PageDownloadProgress>` is a read; `report(pageUrl: String, progress: PageDownloadProgress)` is a write. No batching, no aggregation, no business logic.
2. **OCP**: ✓ Interface — closed under modification (the read/write surface is stable). Open under Koin substitution — a future SharedFlow-based or backend-streamed impl can replace the `MutableStateFlow<Map<...>>` impl without touching the use-site.

4. **ISP**: ✓ Two methods — minimum surface for the slice. No `clear(pageUrl)` (the Idle default + per-page Flow scope handle that); no `clearAll()` (sessions reset on screen leave via VM Job cancel).
5. **DIP**: ✓ Pure `:domain` interface; depends on `PageDownloadProgress` (same layer) and `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow` (Kotlin stdlib-adjacent). No `:data` or `:platform` reach.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:domain/commonMain`.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`. `pageUrl` is non-nullable `String`; `progress` is non-nullable `PageDownloadProgress`.

**`data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/reader/PageProgressRepositoryImpl.kt`** (new)

1. **SRP**: ✓ One responsibility — store per-page progress in a single `MutableStateFlow<Map<String, PageDownloadProgress>>` and surface per-page Flows via map projection. Two methods, both 2-3 lines: `report` atomically updates via `.update { it + (pageUrl to progress) }`; `observe` projects via `.map { it[pageUrl] ?: Idle }.distinctUntilChanged()`. 4. **ISP**: ✓ The impl's surface area is exactly the two interface methods — no public utility methods, no exposed state. Internal: one private `state: MutableStateFlow<Map<String, PageDownloadProgress>>` field initialised to `MutableStateFlow(emptyMap())`. The minimum.

**`composeApp/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/common/componants/images/OkHttpProgressInterceptor.android.kt`** (new — Step 6)

1. **SRP**: ✓ One responsibility — wrap an OkHttp `Response.body` in a `ProgressResponseBody` that counts bytes flowing through the response stream and reports `Fetching(fraction)` events to an injected reporter function. Two classes (`OkHttpProgressInterceptor` + `ProgressResponseBody`) + one internal `ProgressSource` ForwardingSource — each with one job: interceptor wraps responses; ProgressResponseBody delegates to the wrapped body but installs the counting Source; ProgressSource counts bytes via `read()` override and throttles reports.
2. **OCP**: ✓ The `reporter: (url: String, progress: PageDownloadProgress) -> Unit` callback is a structural function type — the interceptor is closed under modification but open under report-target substitution (today the repo's `report` method-reference; future telemetry or logging sinks substitute trivially). The 50ms / 1% throttle gate is a constant pair (`THROTTLE_MS = 50L`, `THROTTLE_TENTHOUSANDTHS = 100`) at file scope — changing them requires changing the constants but no behaviour reshuffling.
3. **LSP**: ✓ Implements `okhttp3.Interceptor` (single-method interface) and extends `okhttp3.ResponseBody` (abstract class) + `okio.ForwardingSource` (Okio's helper). Each substitution honours its parent contract: `intercept` returns a `Response`; `ResponseBody` overrides `contentType` / `contentLength` / `source` to delegate to the wrapped body; `ForwardingSource.read(sink, byteCount)` returns the byte count read from the delegate.
4. **ISP**: ✓ The interceptor exposes one method (`intercept`); the response body exposes three (`contentType` / `contentLength` / `source`); the source exposes one (`read`). All inherited from the OkHttp / Okio interfaces — no method addition beyond what each parent requires.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Depends on OkHttp (`Interceptor`, `Response`, `ResponseBody`, `Interceptor.Chain`) and Okio (`Source`, `ForwardingSource`, `Buffer`, `buffer()`) — both Android-platform-appropriate libraries already in the `:composeApp/androidMain` classpath. The reporter is an injected callback (DIP-friendly — the interceptor doesn't know about the `:data` repo).
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:composeApp/androidMain`. Android-only by design (the slice scopes per-byte progress to Android in Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageprogress; iOS / Desktop ktor3 is deferred to a follow-on slice).
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`. `contentLength` is an `Int` (-1 sentinel for unknown, handled by the `if (total > 0L)` guard before computing fraction); `bytesRead` is a `Long` accumulator; the throttle gates use `Int` tenThousandths comparison (`(fraction * 10_000).toInt()`) to dodge Float equality fuzz; the timing gate uses `System.currentTimeMillis()` (monotonic enough for throttle purposes; not used for absolute timing).
8. **Naming**: ✓ `OkHttpProgressInterceptor` is precise (says exactly what it is and where it plugs in). `ProgressResponseBody` mirrors OkHttp's own naming (`RequestBody`, `ResponseBody`); `ProgressSource` is the role-name for the inner counting source. The constants `THROTTLE_MS` / `THROTTLE_TENTHOUSANDTHS` use SHOUT_CASE per Kotlin style.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ ~35-line class-level KDoc on `OkHttpProgressInterceptor` covers the slice phase, the application-level interceptor choice (vs network-level — application-level fires once per request including redirects, network-level fires per network hop including redirects to a CDN), the 50ms / 1% throttle gate rationale (without the gate, every `read()` of an 8KB buffer fires a report — 200+ reports per page kills `MutableStateFlow.update` perf), the Int tenThousandths comparison rationale (Float equality fuzz makes naive `lastFraction != fraction` always fire), and the cross-reference to `PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt` for the wiring. `ProgressResponseBody` and `ProgressSource` each have brief class KDoc covering their delegation pattern.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable via an in-memory OkHttp client with a `MockWebServer`; assert the reporter receives `Fetching(fraction)` events with monotonically-increasing fractions during the response body read, and that the gate suppresses high-frequency calls (assert ≤ N events for an M-byte download).

## Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageprogress.ktor3 — per-byte progress on iOS + Desktop

Follow-on to Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageprogress. Where the parent slice landed per-byte fraction on Android via an OkHttp interceptor (the Coil-OkHttp path) + per-request Coil listener (Started / Complete / Failed everywhere), this slice closes the iOS + Desktop gap by porting the byte-counting posture to the ktor3 client used by `coil-network-ktor3`. The `:domain` typed progress, `:data` MutableStateFlow<Map<...>> repo, `:presentation` `pageProgress` state field, and `:ui` per-request listener + determinate placeholder branch — all from the parent slice — carry through unchanged; this slice only adds emitters at the iOS (Darwin) and Desktop (CIO) HTTP-client layer.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §80.1 — strategy (`responsePipeline.intercept(HttpResponsePipeline.Receive)` chosen over per-request `onDownload` (Coil owns the `HttpRequestBuilder` internally; no per-request hook) and `createClientPlugin { onResponse }` (fires after body fully read; useless for incremental counting)).
- §80.2 — byte counting via writer channel bridge (`writer(context.coroutineContext) { ... }`-built bridge wraps the upstream `ByteReadChannel`; 8KB buffer pumps bytes through `readAvailable` → `writeFully` while incrementing `bytesRead`; cancellation cascades cooperatively via the `HttpClientCall`'s coroutine context).
- §80.3 — throttle parity with Android (`THROTTLE_MS = 50L` + `THROTTLE_TENTHOUSANDTHS = 100` (= 1%); `TimeSource.Monotonic.markNow()` for KMP-portable wall-clock vs Android's `System.currentTimeMillis`; emits at most ~20 ticks/sec/page; when `contentLength <= 0` the fraction stays `null` and the gate fires only on the 50ms timer — matches Android's `InProgress(null)` "bytes flowing" signal).
- §80.4 — no-engine `HttpClient { }` form (engine resolved via JVM ServiceLoader on Desktop / K/N link-time on iOS, both via `:shared`'s transitive `ktor-client-cio` (Desktop) / `ktor-client-darwin` (iOS); no engine dep declared in `:composeApp`).
- §80.5 — Koin resolution via `KoinPlatform.getKoin()` (the JVM-only `object GlobalContext : KoinContext` is published only by `koin-core-jvm`; the KMP-portable accessor is `org.koin.mp.KoinPlatform.getKoin()` which delegates to `KoinPlatformTools.defaultContext().get()` and returns the same singleton; iOS and Desktop actuals both use this path).
- §80.6 — block-and-ask trigger #1 audit (Coil 3.4.0's default ktor3 `HttpClient()` is vanilla — no plugins, no custom timeouts, no User-Agent; trigger NOT met. Load-bearing iOS/Desktop image-quality fixes (`HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder`, `maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL)`, `CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor`, Android `OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory(callFactory = ...)` pin, `AvifDecoderCoil`, lifted RGB_565/allowHardware Android hints) live at the `ImageLoader`-component layer (Coil's `decoderFactories` and `components`), NOT the HTTP-client layer; orthogonal to the ktor3 swap and untouched).
- §80.7 — files (3 source commits enumerated, all ≤5 files per commit).
- §80.8 — deferrals (no Darwin-engine streaming-aggregation polish — if iOS smoke testing reveals visible "0% jumps to 100%" the follow-on slice swaps engines or falls back to indeterminate; no Desktop OkHttp engine swap; both out of scope this slice).

### Files

Three source commits (plus the plan commit and this close-out):

- `2db6937` — plan + commit roadmap (1 file: new `PLAN_pageprogress_ktor3.md`).
- `7e8c2b2` — common helper (1 file: new `KtorPageProgressObserver.kt`).
- `3ba3209` — iOS actual (1 file: modified `PlatformNetworkFetcher.ios.kt`).
- `26faea2` — Desktop actual (1 file: modified `PlatformNetworkFetcher.desktop.kt`).

### Per-file SOLID checklist

**`composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/common/componants/images/KtorPageProgressObserver.kt`** (new — Step 2)

1. **SRP**: ✓ One responsibility — wrap a ktor3 `HttpClient`'s response body so per-byte reads emit `PageDownloadProgress.InProgress(fraction)` ticks via an injected reporter callback. One extension function `HttpClient.installPageProgressObserver(reporter)`; one pipeline interceptor on `HttpResponsePipeline.Receive`; one `writer { ... }`-built bridge channel inside the interceptor; one read/count/throttle/emit loop inside the bridge. Body-length sniffing, throttling, and channel forwarding all serve the single rule. No request-scope concerns (URL identification comes from `context.request.url`); no UI policy (just emits via the callback); no domain-model construction beyond `PageDownloadProgress.InProgress(fraction)`.
2. **OCP**: ✓ The `reporter: (url: String, status: PageDownloadProgress) -> Unit` callback is a structural function type — closed under modification (the throttle constants and pipeline phase are file-local), open under reporter substitution (today the Koin-resolved repo's `report` method-reference; future telemetry or logging sinks substitute trivially). Adding a new pipeline phase or a new emission variant in `:domain` does not change this file.
3. **LSP**: ✓ N/A (top-level extension function; no inheritance).
4. **ISP**: ✓ The reporter callback is the absolute-minimum signal needed (URL string + sealed-interface status). No "ktor response handle" parameter (would couple the reporter to ktor); no "page" parameter (would require the helper to know `:domain`'s `Page` type). The function's single receiver (`HttpClient`) and single parameter (reporter) is the minimum surface.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Depends on ktor3 (`HttpClient`, `HttpResponsePipeline.Receive`, `HttpResponseContainer`, `contentLength`, `ByteReadChannel`, `readAvailable`, `writeFully`, `writer`) + `kotlin.time.TimeSource` + `:domain`'s `PageDownloadProgress`. No `:data` (the helper doesn't know about `PageProgressRepository`), no `:presentation`, no `:ui`, no `:platform`, no `:shared` reach. The callback shape keeps the helper from reaching into the `:data` impl directly.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:composeApp/commonMain`. Same layer as the existing Android `OkHttpProgressInterceptor.android.kt` (which is `:composeApp/androidMain`). KMP-portable because `writer { ... }`, `responsePipeline`, `ByteReadChannel`, and `TimeSource.Monotonic` are all available on commonMain.
7. **No banned features**: ✓ No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread`. The `body !is ByteReadChannel` type-guard uses safe smart-casting; `context.response.contentLength() ?: -1L` uses Elvis for the unknown-length sentinel; `total > 0L` gates the fraction computation; `coerceIn(0f, 1f)` caps the fraction at the contract bounds; the throttle uses Int tenThousandths comparison to dodge Float equality fuzz; the timing gate uses `TimeSource.Monotonic` (no `System.currentTimeMillis()` on the KMP common path).
8. **Naming**: ✓ `installPageProgressObserver` reads as the action it performs ("install the page progress observer on this client"). `THROTTLE_MS` / `THROTTLE_TENTHOUSANDTHS` / `BUFFER_SIZE` use SHOUT_CASE per Kotlin const-val style. Local variables (`scope`, `total`, `url`, `wrapped`, `buf`, `read`, `lastTen`, `lastMark`, `n`, `fraction`, `tenK`, `timeElapsed`, `fractionAdvanced`) each name what they hold precisely.
9. **KDoc**: ✓ 76-line file-level KDoc covers (a) slice phase + parity with the Android OkHttp interceptor, (b) strategy choice — `responsePipeline.intercept(Receive)` over `onDownload` and `createClientPlugin { onResponse }`, (c) throttle constants (50ms + 1% tenThousandths) with the rationale for each gate, (d) `contentLength` unknown behaviour (`InProgress(null)` ticks throttled at 50ms only — "bytes flowing" signal matching Android), (e) cancellation safety via `writer` coroutine context inheritance, (f) lifecycle bookend reporting (this helper emits only `InProgress`; the Coil per-request listener attached at the `:ui` site handles `Started`/`Complete`/`Failed` — the state machine stays total without this helper duplicating those edges), (g) why every response is wrapped (Coil singleton ImageLoader shares the ktor3 client across all image requests; selective URL wrapping would require a side-channel — premature complexity; the per-request cost of byte counting is dominated by network IO itself), (h) DIP scope, (i) SRP scope, (j) thread-safety (per-call local state in the writer coroutine; the reporter callback is expected thread-safe — the `MutableStateFlow.update` path in `PageProgressRepositoryImpl` is atomic), (k) block-and-ask trigger #1 audit outcome.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Unit-testable via a fake ktor `HttpClient` wired through `MockEngine` that returns a known-length `ByteReadChannel`; assert the reporter receives `InProgress(fraction)` events with monotonically-increasing fractions and that the throttle gates calls to ≤ N events for an M-byte response. The bridge-channel cancellation path testable by cancelling the parent scope mid-stream and asserting no leaked emissions after cancellation.

## Phase 7.x.statistics — Statistics screen rework

First post-Reader feature slice (Task #238). End-to-end port of the legacy Statistics screen (`composeApp/.../features/statistics/ui/screens/StatisticsScreen.kt`, 8 reading-stats aggregates) into the new layer stack: pure-domain `ReadingStatistics` data class + one observer interface + one use case + strangler-fig `:data` impl + MVI surface + `:ui` composable + debug-guarded nav route. Mirror posture to Phase 6.4.x.statistics' `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (same legacy `:shared` `StatisticsRepository` dep) but on the read-side: the rework `:data` impl combines the 8 named flows from the legacy repository into a single `Flow<ReadingStatistics>`. Both routes (legacy and rework) consume the same flows under the hood, so the numbers must agree across the routes for the same user data — this is the primary smoke test.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §81.1 — strategy (strangler-fig over the legacy aggregates; rework `:data` impl reads-only, delegates to the same 8 flows the legacy reader populates; chapter reads in EITHER reader update the numbers on BOTH screens).
- §81.2 — layer-by-layer surfaces (3 new `:domain` files, 1 new `:data` file, 4 new `:presentation` files, 1 new `:ui` file, 2 new + 3 modified `:composeApp` files).
- §81.3 — MVI shape rationale (empty `StatisticsIntent` / `StatisticsEffect` sealed interfaces; OCP-friendly over `Nothing`-parameterised alternative; `handle()` is no-op `when {}` over the trivially-exhaustive empty hierarchy).
- §81.4 — why `init {}` collector (no `OnEnter` — the screen has no toggles / no per-screen state to gate observation on; matches `ReaderViewModel` observers pattern; `viewModelScope` ensures cancel-on-cleared).
- §81.5 — read-duration formatting (pre-formatted String `"Xh Ym"` from legacy `readDurationFlow` reused verbatim; crossover correctness + don't-duplicate-i18n-TODO rationale).
- §81.6 — `:ui` minimal-dep posture (icons omitted — `:ui` deliberately excludes `compose.materialIconsExtended`; matches `LibraryScreen` / `DetailsScreen` / `ReaderScreen` posture).
- §81.7 — loading-state branch (`isLoading = true` default + `CircularProgressIndicator` until first emission; avoids one-frame "all zeros" flash on cold start).
- §81.8 — files (5 source commits enumerated, all ≤5 files per commit; commit 6 at the cap).
- §81.9 — deferrals (no i18n lift; no per-manga / per-day granularity; no "Clear read time" action; no chart / graph rendering; no nav graph route-swap — Phase 9.x is its own slice).

### Files

Five source commits (plus the plan commit and this close-out):

- `fdc9c8a` — plan + commit roadmap (1 file: new `PLAN_statistics.md`).
- `a38f302` — `:domain` foundation (3 files: new `ReadingStatistics.kt` + `ReadingStatisticsRepository.kt` + `ObserveReadingStatisticsUseCase.kt`).
- `2748c17` — `:data` strangler-fig impl (1 file: new `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt`).
- `9417b1a` — `:presentation` MVI surface (4 files: new `StatisticsState.kt` + `StatisticsIntent.kt` + `StatisticsEffect.kt` + `StatisticsViewModel.kt`).
- `70ec958` — `:ui` composable (1 file: new `StatisticsScreen.kt`).
- `190cb81` — `:composeApp` Koin + nav (5 files at the cap: new `StatisticsReworkModule.kt` + new `StatisticsReworkScreenRoute.kt` + modified `ReworkModules.kt` + modified `Screen.kt` + modified `App.kt`).
