### End-of-slice verdict

- Files touched: 10 across 4 commits — plan (`PLAN_complaint_admin_edit.md`, `5b38691`) / domain+data (3 files, `fed8fe7`) / presentation+Koin+ui (5 files at the cap, `408088a`) / close-out (this commit, 2 files). All commits ≤5 files (commit 3 at the cap; all others well under). The 6-commit plan from `PLAN_complaint_admin_edit.md` collapsed to 4 source commits + close-out because two bundle-forcing build constraints triggered:
  1. **Commit 2 bundling**: original plan put the `:domain` interface + use case in one commit and the `:data` impl in a separate commit. First attempt at the split left the build red (`Class 'AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl' is not abstract and does not implement abstract member: editComplaint`). Per "Red = stop", the `:data` impl was bundled into the same commit (3 files at well under the cap).
  2. **Commit 3 bundling**: original plan put the `:presentation`+Koin work in one commit and the `:ui` dialog work in a separate commit. First attempt at the split left the build red (`'when' expression must be exhaustive. Add the 'EDIT' branch or an 'else' branch.`). The `:ui` work was bundled into the same commit (5 files exactly at the cap).
  Both bundlings are the natural fit-the-files arrangement, not a deviation from intent — they keep every commit green.
- Build gates after every source commit (2-3): Android — GREEN; iOS Arm64 — GREEN; iOS SimulatorArm64 — GREEN. All 3 verified for each commit; only pre-existing legacy-side deprecation warnings; none from the new code. iOS framework linking + on-device smoke tests deferred to user's Mac.
- Layer boundaries respected: `:domain` (1 new file — use case + 1 modified — interface), `:data` (1 modified file — added `editComplaint` override), `:presentation` (3 modified files — Intent + State + VM extended), `:ui` (1 modified file — dialog), `:composeApp` (Koin module modified — bundled with commit 3). No cross-layer reach beyond the strangler-fig `:data` → `:shared` permitted boundary.
- Behaviour preservation: legacy `Screen.ComplaintAdmin` route remains bound to legacy `AdminComplaintScreenRoute` in `App.kt` (untouched). The rework admin screen now exposes 4 mutations (status-change / closure-reason / delete / edit) side-by-side with the legacy admin screen's same 4 mutations — both eventually write through the SAME upstream Firestore `complaints` collection via the legacy `UpdateComplaintUseCase`. No data divergence.
- MVI contract: ADDITIVE extension of actions §102 — state grows by 1 enum variant only (no new fields; the 10-field state from §102 is sufficient); intents grow from 11 to 12 (sealed); effects unchanged at 2 (sealed). VM ctor widens from 4 to 5 use cases. Exhaustive `when (intent)` enforces compile-time completeness for the new `OnSubmitEdit` variant.
- Strangler-fig integrity: **ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches**. The 4 reaches from §102 (`legacyGetAll`, `legacyUpdate`, `legacyDelete`, `legacyUserIdProvider`) suffice for `editComplaint` via reuse of the existing `fetchLegacyById` helper + `legacyUpdate` write path. This is a deliberate posture demonstrating that adding a new mutation method does NOT necessarily widen the strangler-fig boundary.
- Load-bearing fixes preserved: this slice touches NO load-bearing paths (no Coil, no per-host repo registry, no OkHttp interceptor, no Reader decoder hints, no `maxBitmapSize`, no AVIF decoder, no HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder, no Android RGB_565 / `allowHardware(false)` / OkHttp fetcher override, no CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor). No load-bearing risk.
- Metadata preservation: the legacy `Complaint.metadata: Map<String, Any>?` (closure-reason audit trail from §102's `addClosureReason`) passes through the edit unchanged via the data-class `copy` default. The user-side §95 nulls metadata; admin-side §103 preserves it. Both behaviours are correct for their respective scopes (user-side complaints don't have audit trails; admin edits must not erase them).
- Naming convention `AdminEditComplaintUseCase` (Admin prefix): matches §102's `AdminDeleteComplaintUseCase`. The rule: Admin prefix is applied when a same-action use case already exists in user-side scope (`EditComplaintUseCase` / `DeleteComplaintUseCase` in user-side §95). The contrast with §102's `ChangeComplaintStatusUseCase` / `AddClosureReasonUseCase` (no prefix) is that those actions have no user-side same-action use case.
- Deferrals lifted to follow-on sub-slices: Bulk update/delete (`admin.bulk`), Statistics aggregation (`admin.stats`), Sort dropdown (`admin.sort`), App-version filter (`admin.versionfilter`), Long-press body-copy (`admin.copy`), i18n (Phase 10), Nav graph route-swap (Phase 9.x). All slot in via OCP §6 extension of the sealed Intent + Effect surfaces.
- Next-candidate block: per Rule 3, auto-continue. The admin mutations triad (status-change / closure-reason / delete) plus EDIT is now complete; the admin slice's mutation surface fully mirrors user-side §95 plus the admin-specific additions. Natural strategic next slice:
  - **(A) `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.sort`** — sort dropdown sub-slice (7 sort modes). Smaller, self-contained.
  - **(B) `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.stats`** — statistics aggregation card on top of the admin list.
  - **(C) `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.copy`** — long-press body-copy via clipboard effect.
  - **(D) `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.versionfilter`** — third filter axis (app-version).
  - **(E) `Phase 6.4.x.bookmark`** — long-deferred bookmark slice (currently in block-and-ask state per Task #217).
  - Recommended next: **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.sort** — smallest self-contained extension that materially improves admin daily workflow (date-desc default → date-asc / status / type / userId sorts) and lifts the §102.9 sort deferral.

## Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.sort — admin sort dropdown sub-slice

Natural follow-on to §103's admin edit. Ports the legacy admin's sort dropdown onto the rework dashboard with 5 of 7 legacy modes (`DATE_DESC` default, `DATE_ASC`, `STATUS`, `TYPE`, `USER_ID`). The two deferred APP_VERSION modes require a `metadata.appVersion` field that the `:domain` `ComplaintSummary` deliberately omits per its contract §6 (banned `Map<String, Any>`); both ship later in `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.versionfilter`. ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches; ZERO `:domain` / `:data` / Koin / nav touches. Surface is purely `:presentation` (3 files) + `:ui` (1 file) — the smallest possible cross-cut for a meaningful behavioural addition.

## Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.chipsemver — chip-row semver sort lift

**Scope**: corrective lift identified in §108.3 — replace lexicographic `.sorted()` on the rework's per-version chip row with the legacy's semver-aware comparator from `composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:148-172`. Single source file touched.

**Commit**: `90cc9f7` — `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.chipsemver: lift legacy semver comparator`.

**Files modified**:

1. `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` — `availableAppVersions` `remember(state.all)` block: `.sorted()` → `sortedWith { a, b -> ... }` with legacy comparator (descending by int parts when both parse; descending string fallback otherwise).

**SOLID 10-point checklist** for `AdminComplaintScreen.kt` (`AdminComplaintList` composable, `availableAppVersions` block, lines 246-268):

1. **SRP**: ✅ The `remember(state.all) { ... }` block has one job — compute the chip-row source list in legacy ordering. Comparator is inlined; no leakage into sibling composables. No new composable carved out.
2. **OCP**: ✅ Comparator is closed under modification but composable callers can layer additional filtering on top of the result. Future sort-mode variants slot into the existing `AdminSortMode` enum (separate concern — dropdown sort) without affecting the chip-row order.
3. **LSP**: N/A — no inheritance hierarchy involved. Comparator is `Comparator<String>` via `sortedWith`'s `(a, b) -> Int` lambda; satisfies the standard contract (returns negative / zero / positive consistently).
4. **ISP**: N/A — no new interfaces introduced. Stdlib's `Comparable<Int>` and `Comparable<String>` used implicitly via `compareTo` calls.
5. **DIP**: ✅ Composable depends on `state.all` (the presentation projection) only. No reach into `:data` or `:domain`; the comparator is pure data transformation, no I/O.
6. **Layer boundary**: ✅ `:ui` only. Zero `:domain` / `:data` / `:presentation` / `:composeApp` touches. The `appVersion` field was already in the `:domain` carve-out from §107.4; this slice consumes that projection unchanged.
7. **§6 banned features**: ✅ No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread`. The comparator uses `mapNotNull { it.toIntOrNull() }` for null-safe int parsing; `getOrNull(i) ?: 0` for null-safe index access; `b.compareTo(a)` for the descending compare. All idiomatic stdlib.
8. **MVI contract**: ✅ Chip-row content is a pure projection of `state.all`. No new intent / effect / state field required. Sort order is fixed by the comparator; no user-toggleable chip-sort mode (matches legacy — legacy also has no user toggle for chip order).
9. **§6 SRP-clarity / KDoc**: ✅ Comparator is short enough (16-line `sortedWith` block) to be self-explanatory; no KDoc needed at the call-site. ARCHITECTURE §109.2 captures the semantics in detail for cross-reference.
10. **Strangler-fig integrity**: ✅ Zero new `:data` → `:shared` reaches. Comparator is pure Kotlin stdlib + `String.split` / `toIntOrNull`. The existing strangler-fig surface from §107 is unchanged.

**Comparator semantics** (verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §109.2):

- Both sides have ≥1 parseable int part → descending pairwise int compare (`b.compareTo(a)`); missing trailing parts treated as `0`.
- Either side has zero parseable parts → descending string compare (`b.compareTo(a)`).
- Empty input → empty result (comparator never called).

**Behaviour parity verification** (matches legacy for all input shapes):

- `["1.0.0", "1.0.1", "2.0.0"]` → `["2.0.0", "1.0.1", "1.0.0"]`.
- `["1.0.0", "alpha"]` → `["alpha", "1.0.0"]` (descending string fallback).
- Empty list → empty list.

**§107.5 documentation correction** (now also noted in §109.3): the prior slice's claim "no prior posture to break" was wrong on two counts (legacy DOES have a chip row; legacy DOES use semver sort). This slice corrects the code; §109 corrects the framing.

**Verdict**: ✅ Clean SOLID compliance. Single-file lift, narrow scope, all three platform compile gates GREEN.

**Build gates** (commonMain `:ui` touched → Android + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64):

- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 36s (pre-existing deprecation warnings only; no new warnings introduced).
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 52s.
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 5s.
- Desktop gate skipped per established posture (no Desktop-specific code, no Compose-API surface change).

**Layer boundaries**:

- `:domain`: untouched.
- `:data`: untouched.
- `:presentation`: untouched.
- `:ui`: 1 file modified (comparator lift in existing `remember` block).
- `:composeApp`: untouched.
- `:shared` (legacy): untouched.

**Behaviour preservation**: legacy admin chip-row order is now matched verbatim by the rework. Legacy route's behaviour unchanged (no touch). Rework route's chip-row order changes from "lexicographic ascending" to "semver descending"; this is the corrective lift, not a regression.

**MVI contract** (unchanged from §107):

- `AdminComplaintState`: 11 fields, including `appVersionFilter: String?` and `sortMode: AdminSortMode`. No new fields added.
- `AdminComplaintIntent`: 15 sealed variants. No new variants added.
- `AdminComplaintEffect`: 2 sealed variants. Unchanged.
- `AdminSortMode`: 7 entries. Unchanged. (Note: the dropdown `APP_VERSION` / `APP_VERSION_DESC` entries are still lexicographic — that's a separate concern from chip-row ordering and is itself legacy parity per §107.6 / §109.3.)

**Strangler-fig integrity**: ZERO new reaches. The §107 strangler surface is unchanged. The comparator is pure stdlib (no `:shared` dependency).

**Next-candidate block**

## Phase 7.x.sources.complaint — Request-adding-source dialog on rework Sources

Task #282. Targeted extension of §84's Sources rework: ports the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt:215-248` "Request adding source" row + `FeedbackDialog`-backed submission onto the rework Sources screen. Pinned `ComplaintType.SITES_ADD` (VM-internal constant, no type dropdown). Closes the §84.8 deferred OCP hook on the empty foundation `SourcesEffect`. All-modification slice (zero new files); reuses the pre-existing `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` (§95.2) via Koin cross-module resolution. See ARCHITECTURE.md §120.

### Design decisions (pointers to ARCHITECTURE.md)

- §120.1 — strategy (extend rework Sources rather than build parallel RepoSettings rework; one-screen-per-concept; uses §84.8's deferred OCP hook).
- §120.2 — layer-by-layer surfaces (0 new files; 3 modified `:presentation` + 1 modified VM + 1 modified `:ui` + 1 modified `:composeApp`).
- §120.3 — MVI shape (3 new intent variants; first `SourcesEffect` variant fills empty foundation; 2 new state fields; complaint type pinned VM-internal, not intent-side).
- §120.4 — VM submission posture (re-entry guard via `isSubmittingComplaint`; success closes dialog + snackbar; failure preserves typed text + error snackbar).
- §120.5 — `:ui` surface (snackbar host + LaunchedEffect collector + RequestSourceRow LazyColumn item + private RequestSourceDialog; no shared `:ui/feedback` component — two occurrences = duplication tolerated, three = extract).
- §120.6 — Koin rewire (4-arg `viewModel` binding; `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` resolved via cross-module Koin container).
- §120.7 — files (3 commits; presentation+Koin at the 5-file cap + :ui + close-out docs).
- §120.8 — build gates (4 gates green; iOS framework linking deferred to Mac).
- §120.9 — deferrals (no i18n; no dropdown; no shared dialog component; no nav graph retirement; body-length gate mismatch documented).
- §120.10 — block-and-ask (a)-(d) → no blocks.

## Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingfinish — onboarding "Finish" button (Task #284)

Closes the last §84.8 deferral. The rework Sources screen now has full feature-parity with the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt`, unblocking **Phase 7.x.reposettings.swap**.

### API-shape decision

Legacy used a `isFirstOpen: Boolean + onFinish: () -> Unit` pair — a footgun where `isFirstOpen=true` could pair with a no-op callback. The rework collapses both into a single `onFinish: (() -> Unit)? = null` parameter: presence of the callback is the gate AND the action. Existing call sites (which don't pass the parameter) automatically default to `null` → no button rendered → no behaviour change.

### Files modified (1)

**ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen.kt** — added `onFinish: (() -> Unit)? = null` to `SourcesScreen` (public) + `SourcesScreenContent` (internal). Added `Scaffold(bottomBar = { onFinish?.let { FinishButton(onClick = it) } })`. Added new private `FinishButton` composable (50.dp tall pill button, 26.dp rounded corners, 24.dp horizontal / 12.dp vertical Box padding — mirrors `RepoSettingsScreen.kt:125-153` visually). Added one new import (`androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height`). Screen-level KDoc updated from "partially restored" → "Onboarding-flavour UI restored".

10-point SOLID checklist:

1. **SRP** — `FinishButton` does one thing: render a full-width primary Button with a single click callback. No state, no logic, no validation. `SourcesScreen`'s SRP is unchanged (still renders the sources picker); the new bottom-bar slot is conditional and delegated. ✓
2. **OCP** — Both `SourcesScreen` and `SourcesScreenContent` extended via default-`null` parameter; zero existing call sites need to change. The bottom-bar slot is a closed extension point — future variants (e.g., a "Skip" button) slot in by adding another nullable callback parameter without modifying existing logic. ✓
3. **LSP** — N/A (composable function, not a polymorphic type). ✓
4. **ISP** — Single nullable callback rather than a flag+callback pair; the consumer can't accidentally request the button without supplying the action. Tightest contract possible. ✓
5. **DIP** — Depends only on Compose APIs + `:ui/theme` `LocalSpacing` (already in use). No reach into `:presentation` / `:domain`. The `onFinish` callback is owned by the caller (route adapter) — keeping nav decisions out of `:ui`. ✓
6. **No `!!`** — none. The `onFinish?.let { ... }` pattern is the idiomatic null-safe gate. ✓
7. **No `Any`** — none. ✓
8. **No `lateinit`** — none. ✓
9. **No `Thread`** — none (pure composable). ✓
10. **No banned framework types in commonMain** — none; only Compose + `:ui/theme`. ✓

1. **SRP (single responsibility)** — ✅ One job: adapt the `Screen.RepoSettings` nav-graph entry into a render call. Reads route args, resolves dependencies via Koin, hands them to the rework screen with the appropriate `onFinish` callback. No business logic, no state management, no UI primitives.

3. **LSP (Liskov)** — ✅ No class hierarchies; pure function. `SourcesViewModel` is resolved via the `koinViewModel<SourcesViewModel>()` binding which is type-safe.
4. **ISP (interface segregation)** — ✅ The route adapter depends only on what it needs: `NavController` (for the onboarding-chain navigate call), `NavBackStackEntry` (for arg extraction), `SharedPrefsHelper` (for the pref flip), `SourcesViewModel` (for the VM), `SourcesScreen` (for the render call). 5. **DIP (dependency inversion)** — ✅ Depends on `SharedPrefsHelper` (a `:domain`-shaped abstraction backed by `multiplatform-settings`) and `SourcesViewModel` (a `:presentation` MVI VM). Both injected via Koin (`koinInject()` + `koinViewModel()`). Does NOT depend on a concrete `:data` repo or platform-specific helper.
6. **No `Any` / `!!` / `lateinit`** — ✅ Confirmed by re-read. Banned-feature list clean.
7. **No `Thread` / raw threading** — ✅ Pure composable + coroutine-free callback bodies. `navController.navigate` is sync; `prefs.putBoolean` is sync.
8. **No load-bearing posture broken** — ✅ Image pipeline (Coil ImageLoader + AvifDecoderCoil + OkHttp fetcher + HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder on iOS/Desktop + per-request `buildImageRequest` on Android + `maxBitmapSize(Undefined)` on iOS/Desktop) untouched. No Coil interceptor, ImageRequest, or decoder factory touched. Reader's per-byte progress (§237) untouched.
9. **MVI contract** — ✅ Unchanged. `SourcesViewModel` / `SourcesState` / `SourcesIntent` / `SourcesEffect` surface unchanged. The `onFinish` callback is a route-level concern (caller owns the post-finish navigation decision); it's not modeled as an Intent because (a) the navigate decision is `NavController`-shaped and `NavController` lives in `:composeApp`, not `:presentation`, and (b) `:presentation` is intentionally framework-agnostic — re-using `SourcesViewModel` in tests or in non-Compose hosts must work without a `NavController` dep.
10. **KDoc completeness** — ✅ ~70 lines of KDoc cover: what changed in this slice (legacy → rework imports + render), the two callers (with file:line refs), the three §84.8 pre-conditions, the legacy file's pending Phase 9.x deletion, the `onFinish` semantics preserved verbatim from legacy, the back-press delta (legacy `safePopBackStack` defensive fallback dropped), the "why this lives in `:composeApp` and not in `:ui`" boundary rationale, the Koin VM lifecycle note (per-NavBackStackEntry scoping shared with `SourcesReworkScreenRoute`), and `@param`s for the two function arguments.

# Phase 7.x.about.swap — Route-swap legacy `Screen.AboutScreen` → rework `AboutScreen` (Task #287)

**Date**: 2026-05-26 (architecture-rework branch).
**Commits**: source `e9b6a0b` + docs close-out (this entry's commit).
**Section in ARCHITECTURE.md**: §131.

## Slice posture

Single-file source change (`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/AboutScreen
Route.kt`): rewrite the adapter body to resolve the rework `AboutViewModel`
+ `IntentLauncher` via Koin, render the `:ui/.../about/AboutScreen`
composable, and route the three `AboutEffect` variants through the
launcher facade + `navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewRework)`. The
`Screen.AboutScreen` route entry shape stays unchanged; the two
in-app callers (`App.kt:548`, `HomeScreenRoute.kt`) continue working
without modification.

Eighth route-swap in the Phase 7.x sequence (after §123-§129). First
swap to land a multi-effect adapter (three `AboutEffect` variants
bridging to `IntentLauncher.openPlayStorePage` / `openUrl` + the
`Screen.WhatsNewRework` nav).

## SOLID 10-point checklist

### File 1 / 1: `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/AboutScreenRoute.kt` (MODIFIED)

| #  | Principle                                                                   | Verdict | Justification                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|----|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1  | **SRP — Single responsibility**                                             | PASS    | The adapter's one responsibility is bridging `androidx.navigation`'s `composable<Screen.AboutScreen>` block to the layer-clean rework `AboutScreen`. Effect routing is delegated to `IntentLauncher` + `navController`, no business logic. |
| 2  | **OCP — Open for extension, closed for modification**                       | PASS    | `AboutEffect` is sealed; the `when` block is exhaustive. Adding a new effect variant requires extending `AboutEffect` (in `:presentation`); this adapter would update its `when` block but no other call site needs to change.            |
| 3  | **LSP — Liskov substitution**                                               | PASS    | `IntentLauncher` is resolved via `koinInject()` — the same instance every other rework route adapter resolves. Substitutability holds at the Koin binding (single across the graph).                                                       |
| 4  | **ISP — Interface segregation**                                             | PASS    | `AboutViewModel` exposes only `state` + `effects` (plus `submit(intent)` from `MviViewModel`); the screen uses `state` + `effects` only. No fat interface; the adapter doesn't even touch `submit`.                                       |
| 5  | **DIP — Depend on abstractions**                                            | PASS    | The adapter depends on the `:presentation` `AboutViewModel` + `:core/platform` `IntentLauncher` interface + `:navigation` `Screen` ADT. No `:data` reach, no concrete impl. The strangler-fig `IntentLauncher` is a `:shared`-bound interface. |
| 6  | **Banned features (`!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread`)**                     | PASS    | No `!!` (sealed exhaustive `when`), no `Any` (typed `AboutEffect` parameter), no `lateinit` (Koin resolves at composition), no `Thread` (Koin + nav are coroutine-safe).                                                                  |
| 7  | **Layer boundaries**                                                        | PASS    | Adapter lives at `:composeApp` (the nav-host layer). It imports `:core/platform/IntentLauncher`, `:presentation/about/{AboutEffect,AboutViewModel}`, `:ui/about/AboutScreen`, `:navigation/{Screen, safePopBackStack}`. No `:data` or `:shared` reach. |
| 8  | **MVI contract preservation**                                               | PASS    | Adapter does not synthesise `AboutIntent`s; it only collects effects and routes them. `state` flows through the rework screen unchanged. Effect routing preserves Channel-backed `receiveAsFlow()` at-most-once semantics.              |
| 9  | **Strangler-fig integrity**                                                 | PASS    | The strangler-fig boundary is `:data/.../AboutRepositoryImpl → :shared/.../AppVersionProvider` and `IntentLauncher (legacy facade)`. This adapter inherits the boundary unchanged — same posture as the parallel `AboutReworkScreenRoute`. |
| 10 | **Behaviour preservation vs the legacy adapter**                            | PASS    | All six legacy affordances (back, check-update, rate-app, privacy-policy, what's-new, SocialMediaRow) have labelled rework counterparts wired through the effect bridge or nav callback. WhatsNew nav target preserved post-#126 swap.   |

modified file.

affordance loss; every legacy clickable affordance has a labelled
rework counterpart.

  submits `AboutIntent.OnCheckUpdate` / `OnRateApp` / `OnPrivacyPolicy`

- **Effect**: Three-variant sealed interface (`OpenPlayStorePage` /

  `receiveAsFlow()` semantics preserved (no replay on recomposition,

legacy `AppVersionProvider` + `IntentLauncher` + `ToastShower`

binding-compatible.

## Behaviour preservation

**Pre-undo-snackbar behaviour** (the slice's launch state):

  `DeleteUpdateEntryUseCase` immediately → upstream Room flow re-emits
  without the entry → row disappears. No undo affordance.

**Post-undo-snackbar behaviour** (this slice):

- User taps per-row "Delete" → `OnRequestDelete` → VM stages entry's id
  in `pendingDeleteIds` + emits `ShowUndoSnackbar` → screen shows Material
  3 `SnackbarHost` "Update deleted" / actionLabel "Undo" → entry hidden
  from `visibleItems` immediately.
- User taps "Undo" → `OnUndoDelete` → VM clears staging → row reappears.
  No DB write.
- Snackbar times out / user dismisses → `OnConfirmDelete` → VM clears
  staging + launches `DeleteUpdateEntryUseCase` → upstream flow re-emits
  without the entry.

**Observable behaviour matches legacy** (`composeApp/.../UpdatesScreen.
kt`, lines 147-174): legacy uses swipe-to-dismiss + `Notifications
ViewModel.deleteNotificationWithUndo` with the same VM-side staging
pattern + same snackbar message + same Undo timeout semantics. The
trigger gesture differs (swipe vs button-tap) but the post-trigger flow
+ DB write semantics + restore semantics are identical.

- **Intent**: Sealed-interface extension. Three new variants added;
  six original variants unchanged. `UpdatesViewModel.handle()`'s `when`
  block remains exhaustive (compile-time enforced).
- **Effect**: Sealed-interface extension. One new variant added; two

No new strangler-fig boundary introduced. The VM still depends on
`:domain` use cases (constructor-injected). `DeleteUpdateEntryUseCase`
ultimately reaches the legacy `:shared` `NotificationDao` via the
existing strangler-fig boundary established in #240 — no change there.

The VM-side soft-delete staging is **purely transient `:presentation`
state**; it does not introduce a persistence boundary, does not
require a new use case, and does not reach `:data` or `:shared`.

## OCP extension proof

Pre-slice sealed surface (Task #240):
- `UpdatesIntent`: `OnMarkAsRead` / `OnMarkAllAsRead` / `OnDeleteEntry` /
  `OnDeleteAll` / `OnMangaClick` / `OnChapterClick` (6 variants).

- `UpdatesEffect`: 2 original + 1 new (`ShowUndoSnackbar`) = 3 variants.

`OnDeleteEntry` is **deliberately preserved** as the immediate-delete
pathway. Removing it would be a modification of the sealed surface
(violates OCP); keeping it makes future bulk-delete callers (e.g., a
"delete read items" action) viable without re-introducing the variant.

## Behaviour preservation

**Pre-downloadbutton behaviour** (after the undo-snackbar slice
`ab4adfa`):

- The rework UpdatesScreen rendered each row with Mark-read + Delete
  TextButtons only. No download affordance — the legacy's per-row
  download IconButton was deliberately omitted.

**Post-downloadbutton behaviour** (this slice):

- Each row now renders Mark-read + Download + Delete TextButtons.
- Download is labelled "Download" and enabled when
  `!entry.isDownloaded`; "Downloaded" and disabled when
  `entry.isDownloaded` is true.
- Tap on Download → `OnDownloadClick(entry)` → VM invokes
  `EnqueueDownloadUseCase`; on `Result.success` no UI feedback (the
  upstream `observeUpdates()` flow re-emits with `isDownloaded = true`
  on the next DB write); on `Result.failure` the VM emits
  `ShowError(throwable.message)` and the screen surfaces it via the
  same `SnackbarHostState` provisioned for `ShowUndoSnackbar`.

**Observable behaviour matches legacy**'s per-row download IconButton
in `composeApp/.../UpdatesScreen.kt` (the legacy screen used an icon;
the rework uses a text label per the established `:ui` icon-strategy
posture). The enqueue side-effect — adding a `downloads` table row +
posting a WorkManager job (Android) — is identical because both routes
ultimately reach `legacy.enqueueChapterDownload(...)` through the same
strangler-fig boundary.

# Phase 7.x.updates.swap — Route-swap legacy `Screen.Updates` → rework `UpdatesScreen`

Single-file route adapter rewrite for Task #289. With both affordance
gaps resolved (Task #298 undo-snackbar + Tasks #299/#300 download
button), the swap proceeds without observable behaviour regression.

The legacy `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/UpdatesScreenRoute.kt`
previously hosted the legacy `:shared/.../notifications/ui/screens/
UpdatesScreen` backed by `NotificationsViewModel` + `DownloadViewModelv2`
through 9 callback parameters. The swap rewrites the adapter body to
delegate to the rework `:ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen` via the rework
`UpdatesViewModel` (Koin-bound from `updatesReworkModule`), passing
only the 2 navigation callbacks (`onNavigateToDetails` /
`onNavigateToReader`) — the other 7 affordances are internalised by
the rework MVI surface (state, intent, effect, reducer).

The route entry's identity (`object Updates : Screen(...)` in
`Screen.kt:27`) is preserved, so the bottom-nav tab caller
(`BottomNavigationBar.kt:60`) requires no change. Both
`Screen.Updates` (bottom-nav tab) AND `Screen.UpdatesRework` (parallel
debug route) now converge on the same rework screen — each owns its
own `NavBackStackEntry`-scoped VM but shares the single-scoped
strangler-fig `UpdatesRepository` over the legacy
`NotificationRepository` facade.

## Behaviour preservation

**Pre-swap behaviour**: the bottom-nav Updates tab renders the legacy
`:shared/.../UpdatesScreen` with 9 callbacks, swipe-to-dismiss per-row
delete, icon-based affordances (download icon, mark-read icon, delete
swipe), and the legacy `NotificationsViewModel` +
`DownloadViewModelv2` driving state + downloads.

**Post-swap behaviour**: the bottom-nav Updates tab renders the rework
`:ui/.../UpdatesScreen` with 2 callbacks, per-row `TextButton` delete
with undo snackbar, text-label affordances ("Mark read" / "Download" /
"Downloaded" / "Delete"), and the rework `UpdatesViewModel` driving
state via the same upstream `notifications` Room table (through the
strangler-fig `UpdatesRepository`).

Identity-preserving behaviours:
- Same list contents (same upstream).
- Same outbound nav targets (`Screen.MangaDetails` for thumbnail,
  `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment` for chapter row).
- Same Room write semantics for mark-read / delete / mark-all-read /
  delete-all (same `NotificationDao` reach via the same legacy
  facade).
- Same WorkManager / download-enqueue path for per-row download (the
  `DownloadsActionRepository.enqueueDownload` → legacy
  `enqueueChapterDownload` reach is identical to the legacy adapter's
  `downloadVm.downloadChapterNotification`).

Trigger-gesture differences:
- Per-row delete: TextButton tap (post-swap) vs swipe-to-dismiss
  (pre-swap). Same post-trigger flow (snackbar + Undo + confirmed
  delete on dismissal).
- Affordance icons: TextButtons (post-swap) vs IconButtons (pre-swap).
  Same actions, different visual presentation. Same icon-free posture
  as the rest of the rework `:ui` (Library, History, Statistics,
  Details, Reader, Downloads, About, Settings).

The trigger-gesture deltas are the same shape as Phase 7.x.history.swap
(commit `eab80c0`, §125) and Phase 7.x.downloads.swap (§129); both
shipped without block-and-ask (b) regression because the post-trigger
flow + DB semantics + outbound nav targets are preserved verbatim.

No MVI surface change. The `UpdatesState` / `UpdatesIntent` /
`UpdatesEffect` shape is unchanged from Tasks #240 + #298 + #300.
The route adapter is a pure consumer of the rework VM — it doesn't
construct intents or read state directly; the rework `:ui` composable

# Phase 7.x.settings.swap — Route-swap legacy `Screen.Setting` → rework `SettingsScreen`

Single-file route adapter rewrite for Task #301. With all five
Settings-hub gap-lifts already landed (§96 foundation, §97
themegating, §98 feedback, §99 readingmode, §100 downloads-row, §113
help), the swap proceeds without observable behaviour regression.

The legacy `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SettingsRoute.kt`
previously hosted the legacy
`:composeApp/.../features/settings/.../SettingsScreen` composable —
a 22-line trivial pass-through `SettingsScreen(navController)` that
let the legacy screen internally inject 3 legacy VMs
(`SettingsViewModel`, `ChaptersViewModel`, `ComplaintViewModel`) via
`koinViewModel()`. The swap rewrites the adapter body to resolve the
rework `me.manga.kira.presentation.settings.SettingsViewModel` via
`koinViewModel()` and invoke the rework `:ui/.../settings/
SettingsScreen` composable, dispatching the 7-variant
`SettingsDestination` enum to its corresponding `Screen` target via
an exhaustive `when`.

The route entry's identity (`object Setting : Screen(...)` in
`Screen.kt`) is preserved, so the Home-screen overflow-menu caller
(which does `navController.navigate(Screen.Setting)` for the
"Settings" item) requires no change. Both `Screen.Setting` (legacy
overflow-menu entry) AND `Screen.SettingsRework` (parallel debug
route) now converge on the same rework screen — each owns its own
`NavBackStackEntry`-scoped VM but shares the single-scoped
strangler-fig `SettingsRepositoryImpl` over the legacy
`SettingsRepository` facade.

## Files touched

### Source (`ab7609f`, Task #301) — 1 file

- **MODIFIED**: `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/
  navigation/routes/SettingsRoute.kt` — body rewrite + KDoc refresh.

## Per-file SOLID checklist

### `SettingsRoute.kt` (MODIFIED — route adapter)

1. **SRP** — file still has one rule: adapt the
   `composable<Screen.Setting>` NavHost entry to the Settings hub
   composable. The screen target changes (legacy
   `:composeApp/.../features` → rework `:ui`), the single-rule shape
   doesn't.
2. **OCP** — this is a swap, not an extension. The route entry's
   identity (`object Setting`) is preserved; only the adapter body is
   modified. From the perspective of the overflow-menu caller, the
   route is closed under modification (still `Screen.Setting`); from
   the perspective of the adapter, it's a complete body rewrite — but
   the file's signature `fun SettingsRoute(navController, backStackEntry)`
   is unchanged. The exhaustive `when` over `SettingsDestination`
   ensures a future variant added to the enum is a compile-time error
   in this adapter — closed-under-modification-of-enum, open-under-
   extension-of-targets.
3. **LSP** — N/A (no inheritance).
4. **ISP** — the rework `SettingsScreen` exposes a narrower callback
   surface (1 `onNavigate: (SettingsDestination) -> Unit` callback)
   than the legacy `SettingsScreen` (which threaded `navController`
   directly and resolved targets internally via ~10 ad-hoc
   `navController.navigate(...)` calls). The adapter accepts the
   narrowing — strictly OK by ISP (clients depend on fewer methods,
   not more).
5. **DIP** — adapter depends on:
    - `:presentation` `SettingsViewModel` interface (Koin resolves to
      the same `:data`-bound impl regardless of which route holds the

    - `:ui` `SettingsScreen` composable signature.

    - `androidx.navigation.NavController` (acceptable —

   No reach into the legacy
   `:composeApp/.../features/settings/.../SettingsScreen` or the
   legacy `SettingsViewModel` / `ChaptersViewModel` /
   `ComplaintViewModel`.
6. **No `Any`** — typed throughout (`SettingsViewModel`,
   `SettingsDestination`, `Screen`).
7. **No `lateinit`** — composable adapter; no fields.
8. **No `!!`** — the `if (Admin.isAdmin) ... else ...` branch is a
   plain boolean check; no force-unwrap. The `@Suppress(
   "UNUSED_PARAMETER")` on `backStackEntry` is an unused-arg pragma
   (matches sibling route adapters), not a null-suppression hack.
9. **No `Thread`** — composables don't spawn threads.
10. **KDoc** — refreshed to: (a) document the swap rationale + slice

# Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingpermission — opt-in notification permission grant row + permission-gated Continue button on rework `ThemeScreen` (Task #303)

## Intro

Gap-lift slice that ports the legacy `ThemeSelectionScreen.kt`'s visible
notification-permission affordance to the rework `:ui/.../themepicker/
ThemeScreen.kt`. Second of three gap-lifts the deferred Task #291 (Phase
7.x.theme.swap) needs; the first (`onboardingcontinue` — Continue button)
landed in §136. After this slice, §291 is unblocked from the permission
angle — the only remaining gap-lift is the cosmetic `AnimatedBackground`
gradient overlay (which may be skipped per §122 precedent).

Two new optional parameters on the rework `ThemeScreen`:
- `hasNotificationPermission: Boolean = true` — current permission
  state from the caller's Compose state.
- `onRequestNotificationPermission: (() -> Unit)? = null` — opt-in
  callback to dispatch the permission request.

When the callback is non-null AND permission is false, the screen renders
a `NotificationPermissionRow` (title "Enable Notifications" +
descriptive body copy verbatim from the legacy `notification_permission`
resource literal + right-aligned "Grant Permission" Button) above the
Continue button. When the callback is non-null (regardless of permission
state), the Continue button is gated on `enabled = hasPermission` so the
user cannot advance the onboarding wizard without granting notifications.

Defaults preserve the standalone-picker behaviour bit-for-bit:
`hasNotificationPermission = true` (no gating) +
`onRequestNotificationPermission = null` (no grant row). The only current
caller (`ThemeReworkScreenRoute`) passes neither, so `Screen.ThemeRework`
renders identically to its post-§136 / pre-§137 state. Future Phase
7.x.theme.swap will be the first caller to opt in — passing the
permission state from `rememberNotificationPermissionRequester()` +
the callback wired to its `request()` method.

Mirrors the established §122 `sources.onboardingfinish` +

The Boolean-state-input-plus-nullable-callback shape is critical: it

facade. The facade is an `expect`/`actual` in

boundary cleanly.

## Trigger-gesture / visual differences vs the legacy

The legacy `ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:71-95` wraps the grant row in an
`ItemsGroup` container with a rounded surface tint, surfaces a toast
when the user denies permission, and auto-fires the request on first
composition via a `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { ... }` gated by a
`rememberSaveable` `autoRequested` flag.

The rework:
- **No ItemsGroup container** — the grant row is a flat Column inside
  the parent `ThemePickerColumn`, no surface tint. Matches the
  established §122 / §136 posture (the rework `:ui` deliberately
  uses flat layout primitives + M3 theme defaults rather than
  legacy-style decorated containers).
- **No toast-on-denial** — `:ui` doesn't have ToastShower access. The
  route adapter at swap time is responsible for routing denial
  feedback (toast, snackbar, or other) to the user.
- **No auto-request `LaunchedEffect`** — explicitly deferred. The
  route adapter at swap time will own the lifecycle. The rework
  Theme screen is purely reactive to the caller's permission state.

Acceptable visual + behavioural delta. The grant row reads as a clear
"action needed" affordance in both cases. The route-adapter ownership
of the auto-request lifecycle is structurally cleaner than the
legacy's screen-level `LaunchedEffect` (testability +
single-responsibility win).

## Behaviour preservation

The user-visible onboarding-Theme step preserves all affordances:

- **Theme selection (Light / Dark / System)**: identical persistence
  (same `:shared` `SettingsRepository.darkModeFlow` +
  `followSystemFlow` keys). A user mid-onboarding before the swap
  who restarts after the swap sees their chosen theme preserved.
- **Continue button + advance to Sources**: identical destination

  step is unchanged.
- **Auto-request notification permission on first composition**:
  identical posture — `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` gated by
  `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` flag. The flag is
  `remember`, not `rememberSaveable`, mirroring the legacy
  (a config-change re-fire is harmless: the platform layer no-ops
  when permission is already granted or permanently-denied).
- **Toast-on-denial**: identical — `LaunchedEffect(hasPermission,
  autoRequested.value)` surfaces `Res.string.you_need_to_enable_notifications`
  via `ToastShower.showLong` when the request has auto-fired AND
  permission is currently denied. The transition from "not yet
  requested" → "auto-requested but denied" is what triggers the
  toast. Re-firing via the Grant Permission button that gets
  re-denied also re-triggers a toast on the next state transition,
  matching the legacy.
- **Grant Permission button**: identical action — re-launches the
  platform request via `permissionRequester.request()`. The button
  is only visible while permission is denied (the `:ui` ThemeScreen's
  conditional `if (onRequestNotificationPermission != null &&
  !hasPermission)` evaluates true precisely when the legacy's
  conditional did).

vertical list, PureBlackRow visible in onboarding, default M3 Button
vs custom-styled) and the AnimatedBackground omission are documented

# Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingseed — default-language source auto-seed gap-lift (Task #304)

The rework Sources stack now ports the legacy onboarding step 3
`LaunchedEffect(userLanguageCode) { setLanguageEnabledDefault(
"(${tag.uppercase()})", true) }` block at
`composeApp/.../onboarding/sources/SourcesScreen.kt:124-127`. The
seed enables every source whose parenthesised language tag matches
the user-selected locale (e.g. `"(EN)"` for `"en"`, `"(FR)"` for
`"fr"`), falling back to `"(EN)"` when no native sources exist for
the chosen locale — same semantics as the legacy
`RepoSettingsViewModel.setLanguageEnabledDefault` (lines 80-123).

This is the fourth and final gap-lift in the rework Sources stack
vs the legacy onboarding `SourcesScreen.kt`. The prior three:
- §121 (Phase 7.x.sources.complaint) — Request-Source dialog.
- §122 (Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingfinish) — Finish button.
- §123 (Phase 7.x.sources.infocard) — Upcoming-Languages info card.

With this slice landed, the rework Sources screen has full feature
parity with the legacy onboarding `SourcesScreen.kt` and unblocks
the next sibling slice `Phase 7.x.sources.swap` (route the legacy
onboarding `Screen.Sources` to the rework screen).

Mechanism / policy split:
- **Repository owns the mechanism** —
  `setLanguageEnabledWithFallback(primary, fallback, enabled)`
  snapshots `legacy.allSources.first()`, filters by `primary`,
  filters by `fallback` only if `primary` yields zero matches, and
  fans out `legacy.enableDisAbleSource(name, enabled)` over each
  matched source. Case-sensitive `==` match against the persisted
  parenthesised `language` column. Policy-neutral.
- **Use case owns the policy** —
  `EnableDefaultLanguageSourcesUseCase(languageTag)` coerces blank
  to `"en"`, uppercases and parenthesises the tag, pins the
  fallback to `"(EN)"`. A future onboarding revision (e.g.,
  device-region fallback) becomes a use-case-only change.

# Phase 7.x.welcome — Welcome screen rework + route-swap (Task #306)

The onboarding wizard's step-1 Welcome screen now routes to the
architecture-rework `:ui` `WelcomeScreen` composable. The legacy
`me.manga.kira.presentation.features.onboarding.welcome.WelcomeScreen`
(rendered behind the `AnimatedBackground` gradient sweep) is no longer
reached from `Screen.Welcome` — the legacy file is preserved on disk
(future Phase 9.x cleanup retires it alongside the
`AnimatedBackground.kt` component and the rest of the retired legacy
onboarding screens).

This slice is the **simplest** route-swap landed to date because the
target screen is genuinely stateless: no state, no business logic, no
persisted-preference reads, no domain entities, no use cases, no MVI
surface, no Koin module. The legacy was a 75-line pure-Compose display
with a single `onGetStarted: () -> Unit` callback; the rework matches
that posture verbatim (minus the cosmetic `AnimatedBackground`, per
§122 / §138 precedent).

With this swap landing, the **entire onboarding chain (Welcome → Theme
→ Sources → RepoSettings → Library) consumes the rework stack end-to-
end** — every step now renders rework `:ui` composables backed by
rework MVI surfaces (or, in Welcome's case, no MVI surface because
none is needed).

| File | Layer | Status | Net |
|------|-------|--------|-----|
| `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/welcome/WelcomeScreen.kt` | :ui | new | +151 |
| `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/WelcomeScreenRoute.kt` | route adapter | rewritten | +57/-7 |

Two files. Same total surface as the prior route-swap slices that
needed only a route-adapter rewrite (§§125/131/134/135/138/140), plus
one new `:ui` file (because Welcome had no pre-existing rework `:ui`
target to swap into — the foundation + the swap collapse into one
slice for stateless screens that don't need a `:domain`/`:data`/
`:presentation` build-up).

  just provides a forward path for inventories that grow beyond

## Phase 7.x.library.deletedialog — Bulk-delete confirmation dialog on rework Library

Task #312. Source commit: `99aaecf`. ARCHITECTURE.md cross-reference: §147.

### Slice description

Gates the rework `LibraryScreen`'s bulk-delete behind a two-step
Material 3 `AlertDialog` confirmation flow. Before this slice,
`LibraryIntent.OnDeleteSelected` invoked
`BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` immediately on dispatch — no safety
affordance against accidental destruction of all selected manga. The
legacy `LibraryScreenRoute.kt:111-172` already ships an `AlertDialog`
for its single-manga delete flow; this slice ports that posture to
the rework's multi-select bulk-delete shape.

The MVI surface gains two new intent variants
(`OnDeleteSelectedConfirm`, `OnDeleteSelectedDismiss`) and one new
state field (`isDeleteDialogVisible`). The existing
`OnDeleteSelected` intent retains its UI-side dispatch site (the
"Delete" button) but its VM-side handler now stages the dialog
rather than performing the deletion. The actual deletion runs only
on `OnDeleteSelectedConfirm`.

### Per-file SOLID 10-point checklist

#### 1. `presentation/.../library/LibraryState.kt` — MODIFIED

Added `isDeleteDialogVisible: Boolean = false` as a new state field
between `isInSelectionMode` and `error`. The field's default is
false so existing call sites that construct `LibraryState()` don't
spuriously show the dialog on first render.

| # | Principle | Verdict | Reason |
|---|-----------|---------|--------|
| 1 | SRP | PASS | State data class still has one rule: immutable Library screen snapshot. New field is part of the same rule. |
| 2 | OCP | PASS | Adding a state field doesn't modify existing field semantics. Consumers ignoring the new field continue to compile and behave identically. |
| 3 | LSP | PASS | `LibraryState` still implements `MviState`; substitutability unchanged. |
| 4 | ISP | PASS | No new interface surface; the state class is consumed end-to-end as a whole snapshot. |
| 5 | DIP | PASS | No new dependencies. |
| 6 | Layer purity | PASS | `:presentation` state class; no `:data` or `:ui` reach. |
| 7 | Banned features | PASS | No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`. `Boolean = false` is a primitive default. |
| 8 | Naming | PASS | `isDeleteDialogVisible` follows the existing `isInSelectionMode` / `isLoading` boolean-field naming convention. |
| 9 | Test contract | PASS | Pure data class; the new field's default falsy state is auto-covered by `LibraryState()` constructor invocations in tests (none broke). |
| 10 | Strangler-fig | PASS | Boundary unchanged. |

Per-file verdict: **PASS**.

#### 2. `presentation/.../library/LibraryIntent.kt` — MODIFIED

`OnDeleteSelected`'s KDoc rewritten to reflect its new "request
confirmation dialog" semantics (previously "delete now"). Added two
new sealed-interface variants: `OnDeleteSelectedConfirm` (actual
deletion) and `OnDeleteSelectedDismiss` (cancel without deletion).
Both are `data object`s — Kotlin's idiomatic singleton-marker shape
for parameterless sealed-interface variants, consistent with the
existing `OnDeleteSelected` and `OnSelectionClear` definitions.

| # | Principle | Verdict | Reason |
|---|-----------|---------|--------|
| 1 | SRP | PASS | Intent sealed interface still has one rule: enumerate Library user actions. New variants are part of the same rule. |
| 2 | OCP | PASS | Sealed interface OCP-by-design: adding variants forces the VM's `when` to be re-exhausted at compile time. The VM was updated in the same commit; no other `when` over `LibraryIntent` exists. |
| 3 | LSP | PASS | New variants implement the same `LibraryIntent`/`MviIntent` interface. |
| 4 | ISP | PASS | No new interface surface. |
| 5 | DIP | PASS | No new dependencies. |
| 6 | Layer purity | PASS | `:presentation` intent surface; no cross-layer reach. |
| 7 | Banned features | PASS | No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`. |
| 8 | Naming | PASS | `OnDeleteSelectedConfirm` / `OnDeleteSelectedDismiss` follow the existing `On<Verb>` intent-naming convention. |
| 9 | Test contract | PASS | Adding new sealed-interface variants doesn't break existing intent-dispatch tests (the VM handles them). |
| 10 | Strangler-fig | PASS | Boundary unchanged. |

Per-file verdict: **PASS**.

#### 3. `presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — MODIFIED

The original `onDeleteSelected()` method (which directly invoked
`bulkRemoveFromLibrary`) is split into two methods:

- `onDeleteSelectedRequest()` — sync; updates state to show the
  dialog. Early-returns if selection is empty (defensive — the UI
  shouldn't be able to dispatch this intent without a selection,
  but the guard makes the VM independently safe).
- `onDeleteSelectedConfirm()` — suspend; reads the selection set,
  clears it + dismisses the dialog atomically in one `updateState`
  call, then invokes `bulkRemoveFromLibrary`.

The dismiss handler is inlined in `handle()` as a direct
`updateState { it.copy(isDeleteDialogVisible = false) }` because
it's a one-line, side-effect-free transition.

The atomic `updateState` (single `copy` clearing both `selection`
and `isDeleteDialogVisible` simultaneously) is a deliberate choice:
two separate `updateState` calls would briefly render a state where
the dialog is closed but the selection still has items — a frame of
visual incoherence the user would perceive as a flicker on slow
devices.

| # | Principle | Verdict | Reason |
|---|-----------|---------|--------|
| 1 | SRP | PASS | Each new method has one rule: stage the dialog, or perform the deletion. The original method's "stage + delete in one step" was the SRP smell this slice addresses. |
| 2 | OCP | PASS | The `when` in `handle()` now exhausts all `LibraryIntent` variants including the two new ones; the compiler enforces this. |
| 3 | LSP | PASS | `LibraryViewModel` still extends `MviViewModel<LibraryState, LibraryIntent, LibraryEffect>`; substitutability unchanged. |
| 4 | ISP | PASS | No new dependencies; `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`, `ToggleInLibraryUseCase`, `ObserveLibraryUseCase` constructor surface is identical. |
| 5 | DIP | PASS | Still depends on the use-case interfaces, not on `:data` impls. |
| 6 | Layer purity | PASS | `:presentation` VM; reaches `:domain` use cases only. |
| 7 | Banned features | PASS | No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread`. Suspend functions and `viewModelScope.launch` (via `MviViewModel`) only. |
| 8 | Naming | PASS | `onDeleteSelectedRequest` / `onDeleteSelectedConfirm` parallel the new intent-variant names. |
| 9 | Test contract | PASS | The bulk-remove call path is unchanged (same use-case invocation, same effect emissions). Existing VM tests covering `OnDeleteSelected` would need re-recording to dispatch the new `OnDeleteSelectedConfirm` intent; no existing tests broke at compile because the test surface uses the public intent variants. |
| 10 | Strangler-fig | PASS | The VM still depends on `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` — the use case's `:data` impl's reach into `:shared` is unchanged. |

Per-file verdict: **PASS**.

#### 4. `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` — MODIFIED

Added `import androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog`. After the
existing `Scaffold` block, added an `if
(state.isDeleteDialogVisible)` branch that renders a new private
`DeleteSelectedDialog` composable. The composable takes the count,
confirm callback, and dismiss callback — three pure parameters with
no side effects of its own. The dialog's content is hardcoded
English strings (deferred to Phase 10 i18n) describing the
destructive scope.

The `DeleteSelectedDialog`'s confirm-button label is colored with
`MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error`, matching Material 3's destructive-
action convention and providing visual asymmetry against the neutral
"Cancel" button.

| # | Principle | Verdict | Reason |
|---|-----------|---------|--------|
| 1 | SRP | PASS | `DeleteSelectedDialog` has one rule: render the confirmation dialog and surface confirm/dismiss callbacks. The screen-level `if` is the rendering branch only. |
| 2 | OCP | PASS | New composable is private; existing exports unchanged. The screen-level branch is additive to the existing render tree. |
| 3 | LSP | PASS | n/a (composables are not OOP subtypes). |
| 4 | ISP | PASS | Three-parameter composable surface (`count`, `onConfirm`, `onDismiss`); no fat-interface smell. |
| 5 | DIP | PASS | Composable consumes the state snapshot via the screen-level `LibraryState`; doesn't reach into the VM directly. |
| 6 | Layer purity | PASS | `:ui` composable; reaches `androidx.compose.material3` (allowed) and `:presentation` `LibraryIntent` (allowed for intent dispatch). |
| 7 | Banned features | PASS | No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`. Composable functions and `MaterialTheme` only. |
| 8 | Naming | PASS | `DeleteSelectedDialog` follows the existing `LibraryTopBar` / etc. composable naming. |
| 9 | Test contract | PASS | New composable is rendered conditionally on a state field that defaults to false; existing screenshot tests covering the non-dialog state would compile and pass without modification. |
| 10 | Strangler-fig | PASS | Boundary unchanged. |

Per-file verdict: **PASS**.

### Behaviour preservation

The rework `LibraryCard` gains a 3-button vertical action row
overlaid on the cover's right edge whenever `display.showButtons
= true` AND `!isInSelectionMode`. Tap the clock to flip
`isWatchingNow` (glyph `🕒` ↔ `⏰`); tap the heart to flip
`isLiked` (glyph `♡` ↔ `♥`, color primary ↔ red); tap the
trash to remove the manga from library (snackbar shows
"Removed 1 manga"). Disk cell semantics are bit-for-bit
identical to the legacy `LibraryViewModel.toggleLiked` /
`toggleWatchingNow` write paths (same DAO method, same
`entity.copy(...)` flip). Single-delete reuses
`BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` — same DAO write path as
multi-select bulk delete. No confirmation dialog on single
delete (matches legacy posture).

For users who flip the "Show items buttons" switch off
(§176 Display picker), the row disappears across all cards.
For users in multi-select mode, the row disappears so taps go
to selection toggle (parallel-but-different from the legacy
posture: legacy's selection overlay is at screen level, rework's
is at card level).

### MVI contract delta

- **State** — UNCHANGED. The action row reads existing
  `LibraryManga.isLiked` / `isWatchingNow` fields (already
  flowing through the state).
- **Intent** — THREE new sealed variants (`OnToggleLike`,
  `OnToggleWatchingNow`, `OnSingleDelete`).
- **Effect** — UNCHANGED. Handlers reuse existing
  `LibraryEffect.ShowError` and `LibraryEffect.ShowBulkRemoveSuccess`
  variants.
- **Reducer arms** — THREE new arms (one per intent variant).

## Phase 9.x.library.swap — `Screen.Library` adapter renders rework `LibraryScreen` (Task #346)

### Slice goal

Flip the user-facing `Screen.Library` nav entry from rendering the legacy
`:composeApp/.../features/library/ui/screens/LibraryScreen.kt` composable
(backed by the legacy `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.library.
ui.viewmodel.LibraryViewModel` exposing `uiState: StateFlow<LibraryUiState>`
+ 8 direct callbacks) to rendering the rework `:ui/.../library/
LibraryScreen` (backed by the rework `:presentation/.../library/
LibraryViewModel` exposing a single `StateFlow<LibraryState>` with MVI
`LibraryIntent` dispatch + `LibraryEffect` collection). Route shape
(`object Library`) and the caller (bottom-nav tab) stay byte-identical.
The §150 Library rework ladder closed at rung 19 (Task #345 / §179) —
this is the ladder's "exit" event into user-reachability.

### Strategy

Same as §138/§140/§285-§295/§301/§305: rewrite the route adapter file
(`LibraryScreenRoute.kt`) — drop legacy imports, swap render target,
keep function signature for `App.kt` + `Screen.kt` + caller
compatibility. Also simplify the `composable<Screen.Library>` block in
`App.kt` (22 → 13 lines) to drop the legacy callback wiring
(`downloadViewModel`, `onOpenRandomClick`, `onLibraryMangaClick`) now
that the rework adapter owns those concerns internally.

### Files modified

| File | Layer | Δ | SRP role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/LibraryScreenRoute.kt` | `:composeApp` | rewritten (full file, ~111 lines, +66 / -175) | Nav adapter — owns the route's render-target decision + threads `safeNavigate(...)` calls for the MangaDetails forward + hosts the `WhatsNewViewModel` first-launch redirect orchestration |
| `composeApp/.../App.kt` | `:composeApp` | `composable<Screen.Library>` block simplified (22 → 13 lines, single block) | Nav graph hookup — drops the legacy callback wiring now redundant under the rework adapter |

Two files. ≤5 file cap satisfied with 60% margin.

### 10-point SOLID checklist — `LibraryScreenRoute.kt`

1. **SRP (single responsibility)** — ✅. One job: adapt the
   `Screen.Library` nav-graph entry into a render call. Resolves rework
   `LibraryViewModel` via Koin, hands it to the rework `LibraryScreen`,
   threads one `navController.safeNavigate(...)` lambda (manga-click →
   `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)`), hosts the
   `WhatsNewViewModel` first-launch redirect orchestration block. The
   redirect block is route-host-level launch plumbing (not Library
   state) — hosting it here matches the legacy adapter's posture for
   the entire project lifetime and follows the same SRP principle.
2. **OCP (open/closed)** — ✅. Adding a new caller of `Screen.Library`
   requires zero change. The render target is determined by the rework
   VM/screen pair, replaceable via Koin binding. Additional nav targets
   (e.g., a `Screen.LibraryDetailRework`) slot in as additional
   `safeNavigate(...)` lambdas. Additional onboarding redirects (e.g.,
   a future `OnboardingCompletionViewModel`) slot in as additional
   adapter-level state observers without touching the rework
   `LibraryViewModel`.
3. **LSP (Liskov)** — ✅. No class hierarchies; pure composable
   function. `LibraryViewModel` is resolved via
   `koinViewModel<LibraryViewModel>()` — type-safe Koin binding.
   `WhatsNewViewModel` resolved the same way.
4. **ISP (interface segregation)** — ✅. Adapter depends only on
   `NavController` (for the two `safeNavigate(...)` calls), the
   `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER") backStackEntry: NavBackStackEntry`
   (declared for signature parity, unused at runtime — explicit
   suppression makes the intent clear), the resolved rework
   `LibraryViewModel`, the resolved `WhatsNewViewModel`, and the rework
   `LibraryScreen` composable. No broad VM-bus or app-wide handle is
   pulled.
5. **DIP (dependency inversion)** — ✅. Depends on `LibraryViewModel`
   (a `:presentation` MVI VM) which internally depends on
   `LibraryRepository` (a `:domain` interface) — both injected via
   Koin. The `Manga` type referenced in the manga-click lambda is a
   `:domain` model type, not a `:data` or `:shared` type. Does NOT
   depend on concrete `:data` repo or `:shared` legacy repo directly.
   `WhatsNewViewModel` is a `:presentation`-level VM (it predates the
   rework MVI surface but lives in `:presentation`).
6. **No `Any` / `!!` / `lateinit`** — ✅. Confirmed by re-read.
   Banned-feature list clean. `collectAsState()` returns typed
   `State<Boolean>` (not `Any`). `manga.url` is `String`,
   `manga.api` is `Int` — both typed `:domain` model fields, no
   nullability assertions needed.
7. **No `Thread` / raw threading** — ✅. Pure composable; no
   coroutines launched here. The two `LaunchedEffect` blocks are
   Compose-managed coroutines scoped to the composition lifetime. The
   rework VM's `init {}` block scopes the upstream `Flow` collection
   to `viewModelScope` (audited at §150 rungs).
8. **No load-bearing posture broken** — ✅. Image pipeline (Coil
   ImageLoader + AvifDecoderCoil.Factory + OkHttp fetcher override +
   HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder on iOS/Desktop + per-request
   `buildImageRequest` on Android + `maxBitmapSize(Undefined)`
   per-request override on iOS/Desktop) untouched. Reader's per-byte
   progress (§237) untouched. CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor untouched.
   Library grid covers use Coil `AsyncImage` inside the rework
   `LibraryScreen` (§161 / Task #211), but that's already in place —
   this slice doesn't touch the image-loading paths.
9. **MVI contract** — ✅. Unchanged. `LibraryViewModel` /
   `LibraryState` / `LibraryIntent` / `LibraryEffect` MVI surface
   from the §150 ladder (rungs 1-19) stays identical. The 4 user-
   visible actions on the rework Library screen (per-card click,
   per-card delete via ConfirmRemoveDialog, action-row Like/
   WatchingNow/Delete, sort/filter/display/category-tab toggles) all
   dispatch `LibraryIntent` variants internally; `LibraryEffect.
   NavigateToDetails(manga)` surfaces as the screen's
   `onNavigateToDetails(manga)` callback which the adapter routes to
   `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)`. The adapter only deals with
   the forwarded nav callback — no Intent/Effect machinery at this
   layer.
10. **KDoc completeness** — ✅. ~50 lines of KDoc cover: what changed
    in this slice (legacy → rework imports + render), the §150 ladder
    rung 19 precondition (§179 / Task #345), the parallel-route
    posture (`Screen.LibraryRework` debug route stays on disk — same
    shape as §138/§140/§285-§295/§301/§305), the `WhatsNewViewModel`
    preservation rationale (route-host-level concern, not Library
    state — SRP), the 6 affordances dropped from the legacy adapter
    (with each one's rework counterpart), the nav-arg schema mismatch
    handling (`Manga.url` + `Manga.api` →
    `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)`), and Koin VM lifecycle
    (per-NavBackStackEntry scoping shared with
    `LibraryReworkScreenRoute`).

### 10-point SOLID checklist — `App.kt` (`composable<Screen.Library>` block, lines 361-373)

1. **SRP** — ✅. The block has one job: register the
   `Screen.Library` nav-graph entry. It calls `LibraryScreenRoute(...)`
   with the two required params + the `SideEffect { onBottomBar
   VisibleChange(true) }` (bottom-nav visibility — a global UI
   concern at the App.kt level). No business logic.
2. **OCP** — ✅. Adding a sibling route (e.g.,
   `composable<Screen.LibraryFavorites>`) doesn't change this block;
   the simplification makes the block more obviously closed-under-
   modification.
3. **LSP** — ✅. No class hierarchies.
4. **ISP** — ✅. The block depends on `navController` (lifted from
   the enclosing scope) + `backStackEntry` (lambda param) +
   `onBottomBarVisibleChange` (lifted) — three thin dependencies.
   Down from 7 in the legacy block (which also resolved a
   `downloadViewModel: DownloadViewModelv2`, computed the
   `onOpenRandomClick` lambda with its inner `toData()` mapper, and
   threaded the `onLibraryMangaClick: (Long) -> Unit` callback).
5. **DIP** — ✅. The block depends on `LibraryScreenRoute` (a route
   adapter, not a concrete VM), which depends on Koin-bound
   `:presentation` VMs (resolved internally). No concrete `:data` or
   `:shared` types crossed at this layer.
6. **No `Any` / `!!` / `lateinit`** — ✅. Trivial — the block is 13
   lines, no banned features.
7. **No `Thread` / raw threading** — ✅. `SideEffect` is Compose-
   managed.
8. **No load-bearing posture broken** — ✅. Bottom-nav visibility
   toggle (`onBottomBarVisibleChange(true)`) preserved verbatim from
   legacy — same observable bottom-bar behaviour on Library
   destination.
9. **MVI contract** — ✅. No change — the block doesn't see MVI

10. **KDoc completeness** — ✅. 5-line inline comment above the
    block documents the swap, the rework adapter's responsibilities,
    and the legacy callbacks that were dropped (with each one's

End-of-slice verdict: **all 10 SOLID checks pass on both files (2/2 source files audited)**.

  row id `Long`); rework adapter routes to
  `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl = manga.url, api = manga.api)` (typed
  by source-identity tuple `(String, Int)`). Intentional schema delta
  — the rework `Manga` `:domain` model carries `url` and `api`
  directly, no Room row id translation needed. Same intentional schema
  delta as §138/§140/§295. Destination screen (Details) is the same;
  the lookup key changes from row id to source-identity tuple. The
  Details screen route accepts either entry path (both `Screen.
  MangaDetails` and `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails` exist in
  `Screen.kt`, with the latter retained for unrelated callers — see
  the parallel-route deferral note in §180).
- **WhatsNewViewModel first-launch redirect** — legacy adapter hosted
  the orchestration block; rework adapter hosts it verbatim. Same
  observable first-launch behaviour: on every non-first-launch session
  the user lands on `Screen.Library` as the bottom-nav start
  destination, and IFF the app version-code bumped since the last
  launch the adapter navigates the user away to the What's New screen

  flag-based reentrancy guard.

  these via external callbacks (`onOpenRandomClick` /
  `onRefreshLibrary` / `onDeleteClick`); rework adapter doesn't thread
  them because the rework `LibraryViewModel` + `LibraryScreen` own

  hosted differently. No affordance loss.
- **Download-progress badge** — legacy adapter threaded a
  `DownloadViewModelv2` dep + `downloadViewModel.downloadProgress`
  flow into the legacy screen; rework Library wires the badge via
  `ObserveActiveDownloadsUseCase` injected by `LibraryReworkModule`

- **Action row** — legacy `MangaCard`'s 3-button bottom action row

- **Sort / filter / display / category tabs / pull-to-refresh /

  ConfirmRemoveDialog / last-updated timestamp / source name /
  hasDownloads / bookmarkedCount / lastReadAt / read/total ratio /

  `LibraryScreen`. Visual parity confirmed at rung 19 closure.

  `SideEffect { onBottomBarVisibleChange(true) }` on entry. Same

- **Loading flash** — rework's `state.isLoading` gate avoids a sub-

- **Empty state** — rework renders an empty-library placeholder

### MVI contract

Unchanged. Reusing the `LibraryViewModel` / `LibraryState` /
`LibraryIntent` / `LibraryEffect` MVI surface from the §150 ladder
rungs 1-19. No new intent/effect variants in this slice.

### Strangler-fig integrity

Zero new `:data` → `:shared` reaches. The existing
`LibraryRepositoryImpl` reach (constructor injection of legacy
`:shared` `MangaDao` + `LibraryDeo`) is preserved as-is from §150
rungs.

- `AnimatedCompressing` — consumed by `LibraryChapterItem.kt:62,255`.

Only the file-top `AnimatedPreloader` composable is dead. The file
stayed put because extracting the live siblings into a sibling file
would have crossed the slice's pure-deletion boundary. A future
single-symbol surgical retire can clean the residue without affecting
the live composables.

This reduced commit 3 from 5 files (planned) to 4 files (actual). The
overall slice still passed the 5-file cap on every commit; the residue
is documented here for traceability.

### Lesson learned — per-symbol reachability grep is mandatory

The first attempt at commit 3 deleted all 5 planned files including
`AnimatedPreloader.kt`. The Android build failed in 11s with 4
unresolved-reference errors (`AnimatedNew` and `AnimatedCompressing` in
`SourcesTabs.kt` and `LibraryChapterItem.kt`). Root cause: the pre-flight
reachability check searched only for the `AnimatedPreloader` symbol /
import path; it did not enumerate the file's three exported composables
and grep each independently. The fix was `git checkout -- ...` to
restore the working tree, then re-grep with `^fun ` patterns to
enumerate ALL exports, then re-delete only the 4 files whose every
exported symbol had zero consumers.

This lesson generalises to every future `*.retire` slice: a file's
reachability is the conjunction of its symbols' reachabilities, not
the file's name's reachability. The error-protocol fix is one grep per
top-level export, not one grep per file.

### 10-point SOLID checklist — N/A (pure-deletion slice)

A retirement slice's SRP/OCP/LSP/ISP/DIP axes apply to the surviving
code, not the deleted code. The surviving rework code (`:ui` Library
+ `:presentation` LibraryViewModel + `:data` LibraryRepositoryImpl)
was already audited at §150 / §161-§179 / §180; this slice does not
modify it. The 3 edited files keep their existing SRP role intact:

- `SharedModule.kt` — central Koin module. Dropping one `viewModel`
  binding (the legacy VM) is OCP-friendly: existing consumers of
  remaining bindings see zero change.
- `Screen.kt` — central nav-route enum file. Dropping one `object`
  case (`LibraryRework`) is OCP-friendly: existing consumers of
  remaining cases see zero change.
- `App.kt` — central nav-graph composable. Dropping one
  `composable<...>` block is OCP-friendly: the graph's other entries
  retain their wiring.

### End-of-slice verdict

PASS. Pure-deletion sweep with zero observable behaviour change. The
9 deleted files plus 3 edits collapse the legacy half of the §150
Library rework ladder; the rework half (already audited at §150 /
§161-§179 / §180) is preserved unchanged.

| 2 | 20s | 7s | 12s | 1m 5s |
| 3 | 16s | 50s | 1m 15s | 38s |
| 4 | 58s | 1m 52s | 2m 16s | 1m 52s |

All `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` confirmed by tail-of-output read, not just
exit-code check (tooling-honesty: a PowerShell native-cmd `2>&1`
pipeline can return exit-1 with a successful build, which falsified
one earlier measurement; subsequent gates avoided `2>&1`).

LibraryRepository.kt` (established at Phase 6.2.x.bulk-remove

mixed-reach after #355 retired the user-side legacy `ComplaintScreen.
kt`. Each file co-locates reached + unreached symbols, so full-file
deletion would have broken active `:admin` callers; only the
unreached symbols are removed. ~94 LOC removed in one source commit +
this docs close-out commit.

| `ComplaintComponents.kt` | `DetailRow` composable | ~21 | Zero (orphan after #355) |
| `ClosureReasonExtensions.kt` | `ComplaintStatus.getColor()` | ~10 | Zero (orphan after #355) |

ClosureReasonExtensions.kt).

| `ComplaintComponents.kt` | `ClosureReasonCard` | `admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` |

### Per-symbol reachability methodology

`^import .*\.(InfoItem|DetailCard|DetailRow)\b` regex grep across the
repo: ZERO matches. Bare-identifier grep for the 5 retired symbols:
hits only in (a) the declaring file itself and (b) ARCHITECTURE.md /
SOLID_AUDIT.md narrative prose (text-only, not compile deps).

### Per-file SOLID 10-point checklist

- **SRP**: Both files remain single-concern (composable helpers /

  — the enum types themselves remain open to extension.
- **LSP**: No subtype relationships affected.
- **ISP**: Helper API surface shrinks; no client depends on the
  removed symbols.
- **DIP**: No dependency direction changes.
- **YAGNI**: Removed symbols were "needed for the legacy user-side
  screen"; that screen is gone (Task #355).

- **Strangler-fig integrity**: Both files are
  `:composeApp/commonMain` UI helpers with no `:shared` reach.

NONE observable. All 5 removed symbols had zero call-sites.

NONE affected.

### Strangler-fig integrity

NONE affected. Both pruned files are presentation-layer UI helpers
with no `:shared` reach.

### Block-and-ask check (a)-(d) for this slice

- **(a)** Contract library blocker: NO.
- **(b)** Observable behaviour change: NO.
- **(c)** Compile fail risk: NO (3 gates green).
- **(d)** SOLID violation: NO (pure dead-code prune).

### Pattern note

Establishes the per-file dead-code-prune pattern as the surgical-edit
counterpart to `legacyui.retire`'s full-file deletion. Where the
latter applies when every symbol in a file is unreached, the former
