## Phase 9.x.refreshvm.retire — delete unreachable :shared RefreshViewModel (Task #359)

### Slice summary

First `legacyvm.retire` slice — full deletion of a `:shared`
`ViewModel` whose only Kotlin reference was its own Koin
registration. 117 LOC retired + 1 module edit (−8 / +5 net). The
rework consumer path (`LibraryRefreshRepository` /
`LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl`) was already wired and serving the
rework `LibraryViewModel`, so the legacy VM was structurally orphan
before this slice — the deletion is bookkeeping on confirmed dead
code.

### Files retired (1)

| File | LOC | Reach before retire |
|------|-----|---------------------|
| `shared/.../features/refresh/ui/viewmodel/RefreshViewModel.kt` | 117 | Sole Kotlin touchpoint was `SharedModule.viewModel { RefreshViewModel(get()) }` (Koin registration only) |

### Files edited (1)

| File | Delta | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt` | −8 / +5 | Drop `import …RefreshViewModel` + the 5-line `viewModel { RefreshViewModel(get()) }` block + the stale "ported in Phase 10.3 Wave 2A" comment. Replace with one retire-pointer comment naming the rework path (`LibraryRefreshRepository` / `Impl` consuming `BackgroundJobScheduler.observeJobState` directly). |

### Files preserved (verified active reach)

| File | Layer | Why kept |
|------|-------|----------|
| `data/.../repository/LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt` | `:data` | Strangler-fig replacement; already duplicates `REFRESH_WORK_NAME` + `LIBRARY_REFRESH_WORKER_CLASS` constants; serves rework `LibraryViewModel`. |
| `domain/.../repository/LibraryRefreshRepository.kt` | `:domain` | Interface consumed by the impl above. |
| `shared/.../core/jobs/BackgroundJobScheduler.kt` | `:shared` | `expect class` both the legacy VM and the surviving repo impl scheduled against. |

### Per-symbol reachability methodology

Three concentric greps:

1. `^import .*\.RefreshViewModel\b` — sole hit was the Koin module's
   import (removed by this slice).
2. `koinViewModel<RefreshViewModel>` / `by viewModel.*Refresh` /
   `: RefreshViewModel` / `private val .*: RefreshViewModel` /
   `lateinit var .*: RefreshViewModel` — ZERO hits.
3. Bare-identifier `\bRefreshViewModel\b` outside `.md` files —
   matches only the deleted file and its Koin registration.

The rework `LibraryViewModel` injects `RefreshLibraryUseCase` +
`ObserveLibraryRefreshUseCase` directly. No third-party Kotlin
caller exists.

### Per-file SOLID 10-point checklist

For `RefreshViewModel.kt` (deleted):

- **SRP**: N/A — file removed. Prior responsibility ("translate
  refresh button taps into `WorkManager`-equivalent schedule calls
  and observe the resulting job state") is now solely owned by
  `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl`.
- **OCP**: Strengthened — the rework `LibraryRefreshRepository`
  interface remains closed under modification; concrete impls bind
  through Koin and any future replacement (e.g., once the Phase 11
  worker lands) swaps without touching consumers.
- **LSP**: No subtype relationships affected.
- **ISP**: Strengthened — clients (the rework `LibraryViewModel`)
  depend on the narrowest possible surface (`refresh()` +
  `observeIsRefreshing(): Flow<Boolean>`) rather than the legacy
  VM's broader `currentJobId` / `jobStateFlow` / `isScheduled` /
  `isWorkRunning` surface.
- **DIP**: Unchanged — `:presentation`'s rework `LibraryViewModel`
  has depended on `:domain`'s `LibraryRefreshRepository` interface
  since the strangler-fig landed; this slice removes a now-orphan
  alternative implementation, not a dependency edge.
- **YAGNI**: Compliant — the VM existed to serve a legacy library
  route that is no longer reached.
- **DRY**: Improved — the two refresh constants now have a single
  cell-of-truth at `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt:77-78` rather
  than co-existing with duplicates in the deleted VM's companion
  object.
- **No `Any` / `!!` / `lateinit`**: Edit introduces none; deletion
  removes none (the deleted VM was already compliant).
- **MVI surface integrity**: No MVI surface affected. The deleted
  VM never extended `MviViewModel<S, I, E>` — it was a legacy
  `ViewModel` predating the MVI base.
- **Strangler-fig integrity**: PRESERVED. The `:data` →
  `BackgroundJobScheduler` (in `:shared`) boundary that
  `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl` owns is unchanged. The slice only
  removes a now-orphan secondary consumer of the same scheduler.

For `SharedModule.kt` (edited):

- All 10 points unchanged in posture; the edit is a net reduction of
  surface (one binding removed, one stale comment retired, one
  retire-pointer comment added) with no SOLID implications beyond
  what the deletion itself accomplishes.

### End-of-slice verdict

**PASS.** Zero injection sites for `RefreshViewModel` confirmed
across three grep passes. 3 build gates green for the source commit.

### Build gates (3 green; Desktop omitted by design)

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m ✅
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 4s ✅
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 59s ✅

Desktop gate not run: deleted file is `:shared/commonMain` and no
`:composeApp` / `:ui` / `:presentation` source was touched. The two
iOS gates exercise the same commonMain symbol graph that Desktop
would, so red-on-Desktop while green-on-three-others is not a
reachable failure mode for this slice.

### Behaviour preservation

NONE observable. Both the legacy and rework refresh paths schedule
the same `BackgroundJob(tag = "LibraryRefresh", workerClass =
"me.manga.kira.work.LibraryRefreshWorker")` against the same
`BackgroundJobScheduler`. After this slice only the rework path
exists; before this slice the legacy path was already orphan (no
injection sites). The Phase-11 deferral on the Android
`LibraryRefreshWorker` class is unaffected — `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl`
inherits the legacy's exact deferral posture verbatim.

### MVI contract integrity

NONE affected. Deleted VM was pre-MVI legacy and not in the rework
MVI surface inventory. The rework `LibraryViewModel` (which DOES
extend `MviViewModel`) is unchanged.

### Strangler-fig integrity

PRESERVED. `:data` reaches `:shared` only via
`LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl`'s constructor injection of
`BackgroundJobScheduler` — same boundary as before this slice. No
new cross-layer reach introduced; no existing reach widened.

### Block-and-ask check (a)-(d) for this slice

- **(a)** Contract library blocker: NO.
- **(b)** Observable behaviour change: NO.
- **(c)** Compile fail risk: NO (3 gates green).
- **(d)** SOLID violation: NO (pure dead-code elimination; surviving
  rework surface is a strict ISP/DRY improvement on the deleted VM's
  surface).

No blocks. Phase 9.x.refreshvm.retire is CLOSED.

### Pattern note

Third member of the 9.x retire family — `legacyvm.retire` complements
`legacyui.retire` (file-delete `@Composable` screens) and
`componentprune` (in-file symbol prune) by handling pure-VM orphans
whose only touchpoint is a Koin `viewModel { ... }` binding. The
pre-flight gate (zero injection sites) is the deciding signal —
without it, a Koin binding alone does not certify unreachability.

## Phase 9.x.commonui.retire — drop 5 unreachable presentation/common composables (Task #360)

### Slice summary

Bulk file-deletion sweep of orphan composables under
`composeApp/.../presentation/common/componants/*`. Five files retired
in the source commit (~319 LOC); one further orphan
(`toast/ToastHostState.kt`) deferred to a follow-up to keep within
the 5-file cap. Refines the `legacyui.retire` methodology by adding
the explicit Step 2 / Step 3 declaration-name extraction gate that
prevents filename-based mis-classification.

### Files retired (5)

| File | LOC | Declarations | Prior reach |
|------|-----|--------------|-------------|
| `presentation/common/componants/ItemsGroup.kt` | ~22 | `fun ItemsGroup` | Zero imports; only KDoc-text references in `:ui` rework + route files |
| `presentation/common/componants/flow_chips/ChipsColumn.kt` | ~50 | `fun ChipsColumn`, `fun ChipItemColumn` | Zero imports; only self-decl. `ChipsRow.kt` preserved (active) |
| `presentation/common/componants/titles/SectionTitle.kt` | ~25 | `fun SectionTitle` | Zero imports; bare-identifier matches only `:ui`'s own `private fun SectionTitle` (different package) |
| `presentation/common/componants/list_items/StatsItem.kt` | ~50 | `fun StatsItem` | Zero imports; same as SectionTitle — `:ui`'s `private fun StatsItem` is a different symbol |
| `presentation/common/componants/list_items/SwitchItem.kt` | ~80 | `fun SwitchItem`, `fun PreviewSwitchItem` | Zero imports; only self-decl + KDoc-text references in 5 `:ui`/route files |

### Files preserved (verified active reach)

The reach-survey short-listed 14 candidates initially but Step 3 reach
verification ruled out 9 of them as active. Highlights:

| Short-listed file | Actual reach |
|-------------------|--------------|
| `auto_sized_text/AutoSizedText.kt` | `AutoSubtitleText` actively called by 5+ legacy files; `NavigationBarAutoText` called by `BottomNavigationBar` |
| `sources/RepoIconResolver.kt` | `rememberRepoIconPainter` actively called by `SourcesTabs.kt` — basename grep would have missed this |
| `floating_button/FloatingActionButton.kt` | `AnimatedCircleExtendedFab` called by legacy `LibraryMangaScreen` (mixed-reach; the other 2 funs are componentprune candidates) |
| `images/SourceImageRequest.kt` | `rememberSourceImageRequest` called by 8+ legacy files (Reader, all reading modes, Home, Details) |
| `images/KtorPageProgressObserver.kt` | `installPageProgressObserver` called by iOS + Desktop `PlatformNetworkFetcher` actuals |
| `images/BlurredImageCoil.kt`, `images/ImageWithGradientOverlay.kt` | Pair reached from legacy `LibraryMangaScreen` + `DetailsContent` |
| `scroll/LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt` | `VerticalFastScroller` called by legacy `DetailsContent` |

### Reach methodology (the Step 2 / Step 3 refinement)

Filename-grep alone is insufficient because Kotlin file basenames do
not always match exported declaration names. The methodology now is:

1. `^import .*\.<file-basename>\b` — short-list zero-import-site
   candidates.
2. Extract actual top-level `fun`/`class`/`object` declarations from
   each candidate file (NOT trusting basename).
3. `^import .*\.(<actual-names>)\b` re-grep against the whole repo.
4. Bare-identifier `\b(<names>)\b` scan to catch same-package callers
   (no `import` needed) and exclude KDoc-text references in `:ui`
   rework files describing legacy posture.

Steps 2–3 are the new gate. They caught the
`rememberRepoIconPainter` / `AnimatedCircleExtendedFab` /
`AutoSubtitleText`+`NavigationBarAutoText` near-misses where filename
grep would have produced a false-orphan classification.

### Per-file SOLID 10-point checklist

For each of the 5 retired files (all helper composables):

- **SRP**: N/A — each file had a single responsibility (one
  composable surface or two related composable surfaces). Removal
  doesn't change any consumer's responsibility because there were no
  consumers.
- **OCP**: Strengthened — the rework `:ui` module's `private fun`
  redefinitions (in `:ui/.../StatisticsScreen.kt`) own their own
  evolution under modification; removing the unused legacy duplicates
  ensures consumers can't accidentally bind to the wrong version.
- **LSP**: No subtype relationships affected.
- **ISP**: Strengthened — the legacy helper surface area in
  `presentation/common/componants/*` shrinks by 5 files; no consumer
  depended on the removed symbols, so no client interface is
  narrowed/broken.
- **DIP**: Unchanged — `:composeApp/commonMain` UI helpers have no
  dependency direction implications. `:ui` continues to redefine its
  own private composables.
- **YAGNI**: Compliant — removed symbols were "needed for the legacy
  Statistics / Settings / About / Language screens"; those screens
  are gone (retired in #349 / #354 / #350 / Library swap chain).
- **DRY**: No new duplication. The retired files had legacy
  duplicates of what `:ui` now declares privately; removing them
  reduces apparent duplication (legacy ItemsGroup vs `:ui`'s
  StatisticsScreen-local ItemsGroup) at the cost of NOT promoting
  the `:ui` versions to a shared `:ui` helper module — a deliberate
  isolation decision documented in §192's pattern note.
- **No `Any` / `!!` / `lateinit`**: Deletions remove none (the
  retired files were already compliant).
- **MVI surface integrity**: No MVI surface affected (UI helpers
  only, no state/intent/effect types).
- **Strangler-fig integrity**: PRESERVED. The retired files lived in
  `:composeApp/commonMain` and had no cross-layer reach. The
  strangler-fig boundary (`:data` ↔ `:shared`) is unchanged.

### End-of-slice verdict

**PASS.** Zero import sites and zero same-package callers for all 5
retired files. 3 build gates green.

### Build gates (3 green; Desktop omitted by design)

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 12s ✅
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (combined run, 37s) ✅
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (combined run, 37s) ✅

Desktop gate not run: deleted files are `commonMain` UI helpers; the
iOS gates exercise the same compile graph that Desktop would, so
red-on-Desktop while green-on-three-others is not a reachable failure
mode for this slice.

### Behaviour preservation

NONE observable. All 5 retired files had zero call-sites.

### MVI contract integrity

NONE affected.

### Strangler-fig integrity

PRESERVED.

### Block-and-ask check (a)-(d) for this slice

- **(a)** Contract library blocker: NO.
- **(b)** Observable behaviour change: NO.
- **(c)** Compile fail risk: NO (3 gates green).
- **(d)** SOLID violation: NO (pure dead-code elimination; surviving
  surface is a strict ISP improvement).

### Pattern note

Refines `legacyui.retire` with explicit declaration-name extraction
between filename-grep and reach-verification. Filename can diverge

robust to this divergence. Future common-UI sweeps in any project

After three instances (§191, §193's analysis, §195), the

### Pattern note — componentprune rubric matures (4 instances)

After §158 (ComplaintComponents), §195 (FAB), and this slice (Scroller),
the `componentprune` rubric is hardened to 3 steps:

1. **Identify a mixed-reach file** — file basename grep suggests
   fully-reached (because ≥1 declaration is reached), but per-declaration
   grep proves otherwise. §193 filename-vs-declaration gate.
2. **3-pass grep over each declared symbol** — anchored import + (where
   applicable) injection-site + bare-identifier. Categorize each as
   REACHED / ORPHAN / TRANSITIVELY-ORPHAN (private helpers whose sole
   caller is an orphan).
3. **Surgical Write** — rewrite the file keeping only surviving
   declarations + their imports; preserve everything byte-identical
   (whitespace, KDoc, parameter defaults) except for KDoc cross-refs
   to removed symbols.

Differs from `legacyui.retire` (file-level deletion of fully-unreached
`@Composable` screens) and `legacyvm.retire` (file-level deletion of
`:shared` ViewModel + Koin binding edit).

## Phase 9.x.statisticsdao.componentprune — `StatisticsDeo` `*Once` orphan retire (Task #393)

**Status**: Closed.
**Commits**: `728d6ae` (source), this commit (docs).

### Per-file SOLID 10-point checklist

#### `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/local/dao/StatisticsDeo.kt`

1. **SRP**: ✅ One rule — expose reactive aggregate counts over
   `saved_manga` + `saved_chapters` to the legacy `StatisticsRepository`
   facade. The 7 `*Once` suspend variants violated this implicitly: they
   were a second surface (single-shot reads) for which no consumer
   existed.
2. **OCP**: ✅ Closed under modification — the 7 preserved Flow methods
   keep their exact signatures (`fun X(): Flow<Int>`); the legacy
   facade's 7 `*Flow` properties keep their delegation calls unchanged.
   Open under extension — a new aggregate (e.g. lifetime read count)
   slots in as a new `@Query` method without touching the existing 7.
3. **LSP**: ✅ Dropped methods had no consumers. No substitutability
   contract to break (Room's KSP impl is regenerated from the Kotlin
   interface; the new generated impl satisfies the trimmed contract by
   construction).
4. **ISP**: ✅ Interface narrows from 14 to 7 methods (50% reduction).
   Each remaining method is consumed exactly once by the upstream
   facade — minimal segregation.
5. **DIP**: ✅ `StatisticsDeo` remains an abstraction Room's KSP plugin
   generates impls for; the consumer-side `:shared`
   `StatisticsRepository` facade depends on this abstraction. The
   rework `:data` `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` reaches the legacy
   facade, not the DAO directly — that delegation chain is unaffected
   by this slice.
6. **YAGNI**: ✅ The dropped `*Once` variants were the textbook YAGNI
   example — added as a forward-looking hook ("if you need single-shot
   calls"), no consumer ever took them. Retire on first proof of
   non-use.
7. **DRY**: ✅ The 7 dropped methods duplicated SQL with the 7 Flow
   variants (same SELECT statements, different return type). Drop
   removes the duplication.
8. **No `!!` / `Any` / `lateinit`**: ✅ Kotlin DAO interface; no
   banned constructs.
9. **Banned features**: ✅ None introduced.
10. **MVI contract**: N/A — DAO sits below the MVI surface.

✅ **Pass.** The 7-method `*Once` drop is non-observable from any LIVE
callsite (zero reachers under all 3 anchor patterns). The preserved
7 Flow members exhaust the consumer surface that exists today

## Phase 9.x.statisticsrepository.componentprune — drop orphan `readMinutesFlow` re-export on legacy `:shared` StatisticsRepository (Task #395)

Member-level componentprune on `shared/.../features/statistics/domain/
StatisticsRepository.kt`. Dropped the public re-export property
`val readMinutesFlow: Flow<Int> = dataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow` at the
prior line 44 — a zero-external-reach pass-through whose only call site
was an internal derivation at the prior line 46. The drop inlines the
upstream into the line-46 `readDurationFlow.map { ... }` derivation,
collapsing 2 lines into 1 without altering observable semantics.

### Per-file SOLID 10-point checklist — StatisticsRepository.kt

1. **SRP**: ✓ Tighter — the prune removes a redundant re-export
   indirection. Class still owns "expose the 7 Room-backed aggregate
   flows + the pre-formatted `readDurationFlow` + the session-timer
   start/end API" — one rule, one place. The dropped property was a
   second alias for the upstream `DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow` that
   provided no additional semantics and added one structural layer.
2. **OCP**: ✓ No closed-set assumptions changed. The 7 Room-backed flows
   remain `Flow<Int>` (their cardinality is set by the Statistics screen
   layout, not by this class); the timer API is unchanged. A future
   "expose raw minute-counter on StatisticsRepository" extension would
   re-add the property — perfectly substitutable; the rework is just
   honest about today's actual external surface (the formatted
   `readDurationFlow`).
3. **LSP**: ✓ Class is a leaf type with no inheritance hierarchy; no LSP
   surface to violate.
4. **ISP**: ✓ Tighter — the strangler-fig consumer
   (`ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl`) consumes only the 8 surviving
   public surfaces (7 chapter/entry counters + `readDurationFlow`). The
   dropped wrapper was zero-coupling overhead.
5. **DIP**: ✓ Class still depends on `StatisticsDeo` (DAO interface) +
   `DataStoreHelper` (multiplatform-settings facade); both are
   interface-or-facade abstractions, not concrete persistence
   implementations. No change in dependency direction.
6. **Banned features**: ✓ Untouched — no `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`,
   `Thread` introduced; no `runBlocking` / `GlobalScope` / silent
   `try/catch`. The rewrite at line 46 (now: `dataStoreHelper.
   readMinutesFlow.map { ... }`) uses the same pure
   `kotlinx.coroutines.flow` operators as before.
7. **Layer boundary**: ✓ `:shared` is a legacy module that the
   strangler-fig `:data` layer reaches into via the existing posture
   (`ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` — §192 `:data` → `:shared`
   boundary). The prune happens INSIDE `:shared`'s feature folder and
   does not change the boundary direction.
8. **Naming**: ✓ Names left intact for the surviving 7 Room aggregates
   (mirror the source legacy verbatim — `inLibraryFlow`,
   `chaptersTotalFlow`, etc.). The dropped `readMinutesFlow` wrapper was
   structurally an alias; removing it eliminates the duplicate
   identifier confusion (callers should reach `DataStoreHelper.
   readMinutesFlow` directly if they need raw minutes).
9. **Comments / KDoc**: ✓ Class header KDoc preserved (Phase 8.13 batch B
   migration notes). New audit-header comment added (lines 30-60)
   documenting the drop, the exhaustive 3-pass audit posture, the
   semantic-overlap-with-internal-use rationale, the 9-member LIVE-
   preservation table, and the inlining of the line-46 derivation.
10. **Test seam**: ✓ Class is still construction-time testable with a
    fake `StatisticsDeo` (returning canned `Flow<Int>` for each of the 7
    aggregates) and a fake `DataStoreHelper` (returning a canned
    `readMinutesFlow: Flow<Int>` + a recording `addReadMinutes(delta)`).
    The prune removes one redundant intermediate property — the
    end-to-end emission contract on `readDurationFlow` is unchanged, so
    any existing test that asserts the "Xh Ym" formatting on a known
    minute count still passes verbatim.

### End-of-slice verdict

Clean componentprune. One orphan dropped, 10 members preserved, all
build gates green. Eliminates one structural indirection without
altering observable behaviour. The session-timer half of the class

## Phase 9.x.dao.componentprune.cumulative.rewind (Task #414) — Post-Task #412 DAO orphan rewind audit (NULL RESULT)

### Slice intent

§242's next-candidate block (closing Task #413) flagged cumulative
DAO re-sweep as the #1 priority next-tier candidate after the
12-strong VM componentprune cascade (Tasks #401-#412) closed out the
major `:shared` legacy VM surface. The rewind audit's hypothesis:
**Tasks #401-#412 may have consumed the last external reachers of
previously-gated DAO members, making them new orphan candidates.**

This entry documents the rewind audit's findings + verdict.

### Audit method

3-pass receiver-anchored grep audit across all 8 `@Dao`-annotated
interfaces in `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/local/dao/`:

| Pass | Pattern | Catches |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `receiver.X(` | most common DAO call form |
| 2 | `\bX\b` | bare-name receiver-elision (extension fn bodies) |
| 3 | `::X` | method-reference reachers |

For each DAO member, count external reachers (callers outside the
DAO file itself). If zero, mark as candidate; if zero, also check
intra-DAO @Transaction body callsites (Room's compose-by-call uses
these too).

### DAO files surveyed

- `ChapterDao.kt` — 0 new candidates (post-Task #401 final form
  already optimal)
- `ChapterDownloadDao.kt` — 0 (post-Task #394 final form)
- `HistoryDao.kt` — 0
- `LibraryDeo.kt` — 5 candidates (see verdict below)
- `NotificationDao.kt` — 0 (post-Task #385 final form)
- `SourcesDao.kt` — 0 (post-Task #389 final form)
- `StatisticsDao.kt` — 0 (post-Task #393 final form)
- `LibrarySubscriptionDao` (embedded) — 0

**Total raw candidates:** 5 (all in LibraryDeo.kt). **Actionable
candidates:** 0 (see verdict).

### LibraryDeo.kt candidates — verdict per member

| Method (file:line) | Annotation | Intra-DAO @Transaction caller | External reachers | Verdict |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------|-------------------|---------|
| `getMangaIdByUrl(url)` (line 19) | `@Query` suspend | `saveMangaWithChapters` body (line 38) | 0 | **KEEP — intra-DAO helper** |
| `deleteMangaById(id)` (line 60) | `@Query` suspend | `removeMangaWithChapters` body (line 67) | 0 | **KEEP — intra-DAO helper** |
| `removeAllChaptersForManga(mangaId)` (line 71) | `@Query` suspend | `removeMangaWithChapters` body (line 64) | 0 | **KEEP — intra-DAO helper** |
| `removeAllNotification(mangaId)` (line 74) | `@Query` suspend | `removeMangaWithChapters` body (line 65) | 0 | **KEEP — intra-DAO helper** |
| `removeHistory(mangaId)` (line 76) | `@Query` suspend | `removeMangaWithChapters` body (line 66) | 0 | **KEEP — intra-DAO helper** |

### Why these 5 are NOT prunable (Room compose-by-call rule)

Room's `@Transaction` method bodies **cannot inline raw SQL**. The
@Transaction body is a plain Kotlin function that Room wraps in a
`runInTransaction { ... }` runtime block. The body must compose by
calling other DAO methods, each of which carries its SQL via its own
`@Query` / `@Insert` / `@Update` / `@Delete` annotation. There is NO
Room API for embedding raw SQL inline.

This rule is documented in this codebase's `ChapterDao.kt:27-28`
audit header: *"Room resolves method names within the @Dao scope, so
the LibraryDeo callsite never reached ChapterDao's variant."* The
same rule applies in reverse — a LibraryDeo @Transaction body call
to `getMangaIdByUrl` resolves to LibraryDeo's own abstract method,
which **must continue to exist** for Room to generate the SQL impl.

Removing any of the 5 would cause Room's annotation processor to
fail with "unresolved reference" errors when compiling the
`saveMangaWithChapters` / `removeMangaWithChapters` @Transaction
bodies.

### Visibility narrowing alternative — rejected

Could the 5 methods be marked `internal` to encode their intra-DAO
scope? Rejected:

1. Kotlin interface abstract methods cannot be `private` (impl is
   generated externally by Room's annotation processor).
2. `internal` is theoretically valid for Room DAOs (it's not banned
   by the Room contract), but the YAMI codebase has zero existing
   `internal fun` declarations across all 8 DAO files — checking via
   grep `internal\s+(?:suspend\s+)?fun\s+\w+` returns no matches.
3. Introducing `internal` purely to document a fact already obvious
   from the @Transaction body (the @Transaction method literally
   calls the helpers in plain sight inside the same file) would
   introduce a new DAO pattern variation for marginal documentation
   value. Not worth the structural churn.

**Action: no source change.**

### Per-file SOLID checklist (audit-only — no files modified)

This slice is audit-only — no source files modified. The SOLID
checklist below records the audit's positive verdict on the
*pre-existing* state of `LibraryDeo.kt` (which the audit confirmed is
correctly structured).

#### LibraryDeo.kt (post-audit verdict)

| Axis | Status | Note |
|------|--------|------|
| SRP | ✅ | DAO has one rule: define the SQL contracts for the Library aggregate (manga + saved chapters + their associated notification/history rows). |
| OCP | ✅ | Adding new @Query members would not require modifying existing ones; the @Transaction bodies compose by call. |
| LSP | ✅ | Abstract interface; Room generates the substitutable concrete impl. |
| ISP | ✅ | All members in the same DAO serve the same aggregate; no client is forced to depend on methods it doesn't use. |
| DIP | ✅ | Higher layers depend on this interface, not Room's generated impl. |
| Banned features | ✅ | No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread`. |
| Behaviour preservation | ✅ | No source change — behaviour preserved trivially. |
| MVI contract | N/A | DAO layer, not MVI. |
| Layer boundary | ✅ | `:shared/data/local/dao/` — Room DAO interfaces correctly scoped. |
| Doc consistency | ✅ | DAO members visible in plain code; @Transaction body callsites self-document. No KDoc changes needed (the @Transaction body literally calls the 5 helpers in plain sight). |

### Audit methodology cheatsheet (carry-forward for §245)

For any future cumulative audit, the 3-pass receiver-anchored grep
plus 4 enumeration disciplines:

1. `\.X\s*\(` — call sites by name.
2. `\bX\b` — bare identifier (catches KDoc refs, method refs, type
   names — useful for catching shadowed names).
3. `::X` — member references.
4. **`:app/` enumeration** — always include this Android-only module;
   it has `LibraryRefreshWorker`, `ChapterNotificationHelper`,
   `OnboardingWorker`, and other workers that reach into `:shared`
   facades.
5. **`:data/` strangler-fig enumeration** — search for `legacy\.X` /
   `legacyX\.Y` patterns in addition to `repositoryName\.X` patterns.
6. **`:composeApp/` enumeration** — search `App.kt`, all
   `*ReworkScreenRoute.kt` files, and all `*ReworkModule.kt` Koin
   modules. The Coil singleton image-loader wiring lives in `App.kt`
   and reaches into legacy facades.
7. **Stale `ARCHITECTURE.md` audit-table mitigation** — never trust
   a `LIVE via X.kt:N` table entry verbatim; always re-grep the
   current source to confirm. The audit tables are time-stamped
   snapshots, not live documents.
8. **Misleading parameter naming** — when a `.X(` match is in a
   per-source repo or BaseManga subclass, ALWAYS read the
   constructor parameter type to confirm receiver type. The
   `sourcesRepository: SourcesDao` pattern (BaseManga.kt:36) is the
   canonical example of a name/type mismatch that causes false
   positives.

### Audit methodology cheatsheet (carry-forward for §246)

Additional disciplines learned during this survey (in addition to the
8 disciplines documented in §244):

9. **Named-arg writes vs. accessor reads** — for data-class field
   audits, the bareword `\bX\b` pattern matches every named-arg
   construction (`X = value`) PLUS every type declaration PLUS every
   accessor read. To isolate orphan candidates: grep `\.X\b`
   separately; if it returns zero or near-zero matches while `\bX\b`
   returns 50+, the field is write-only.

10. **`.copy(X = …)` mutation cross-check** — even when `.X` accessor
    reads are zero, a hidden `.copy(X = derived)` rewrite still
    constitutes a write+read coupling that must be flushed. Grep
    `\.copy\([^)]*X` to confirm no hidden mutations before declaring
    a field orphan.

11. **`componentN()` destructuring cross-check** — Kotlin data classes
    auto-generate `component1()`..`componentN()` for positional
    destructuring. If a consumer does `val (a, b, c) = mangaInfo`,
    the accessor reads are positional, not by-name. Grep
    `component\d+\(\)` in proximity to the type name to catch this.

12. **Rework-side disambiguation** — when the rework `:domain` type
    already drops a field (e.g. `Chapter.kt` dropping `chaptersImages`
    or `Source` dropping `siteState`), that's a strong signal the
    field is already known-orphan-from-the-rework's-perspective; the
    audit task becomes "verify whether the legacy type retains it for
    strangler-fig parity or for legacy consumers still in production
    (e.g. legacy Home routing reads `siteState` directly off the
    entity)". Never assume the rework's KDoc claim retires the legacy
    field — verify the legacy consumers.

13. **Serialization-aware pre-flight** — `@Serializable` data classes
    cannot have fields removed without persistence-layer coordination.
    Before pruning any `@Serializable` field: confirm no JSON dumps of
    the old shape are persisted across app versions; if persisted, add
    `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` to the relevant `Json`
    instance BEFORE the field removal.

### Audit methodology cheatsheet (carry-forward for §247)

Carrying forward §245 disciplines #1-#13. Adding new discipline
discovered during this campaign:

14. **Enumerate ALL fields of an audited type — don't stop at "enough
    orphans"** — the §245 survey found 4 MangaInfo orphans and moved
    on; Slice 1's pre-edit re-audit caught 2 additional orphans
    (`artist`, `tags`) that had been overlooked. The cost of fully
    enumerating each type's fields is small (≤17 fields per type for
    the `:shared` domain models); the cost of an undercount is a
    confusing audit→execution mismatch that must then be reconciled
    in the docs (this §246 entry contains an entire section
    explaining the discrepancy). Discipline: for every audited type,
    grep `\.X\b` for X = every field of that type's full declaration.

15. **Audit ALL files of an apparent reacher graph — including
    out-of-scope siblings** — Slice 12's compile gate caught 2
    missed writer sites in `:shared/core/util/data_classes/Handel
    DataClasses.kt` that lived outside the audit's
    `:shared/sources_repositry/` scope. The audit had assumed
    "source repositories construct MangaInfo" implied
    "`sources_repositry/` contains all constructor sites." It
    didn't — `HandelDataClasses.kt` had two factory functions
    (`MangaItem.toMangaInfo` and `SavedMangaEntity.toMangaInfo`)
    that also constructed `MangaInfo`. Discipline: before scoping a
    multi-commit prune, do a final `MangaInfo\(` grep across the
    ENTIRE `*.kt` tree (not just the suspected reacher root) and
    confirm every match falls within your planned slice surface.

### Coupled-dead retirement — `ChapterImage`

§246's discipline #15 (audit ALL files of an apparent reacher graph)
was the new lesson from that campaign. This campaign added a
SYMMETRIC discipline #16 (audit all CALLERS of an apparent
single-anchor type) — see methodology-cheatsheet update below. The
trigger:

- Pre-Slice-2 grep `import me.manga.kira.domain.model.ChapterImage`
  returned exactly 1 site (`HandelDataClasses.kt`), which Slice 2 was
  about to clean.
- Pre-Slice-2 grep `ChapterImage\(` (constructor calls) returned
  exactly 1 site (inside `SavedChapterEntity.toChapterItem()` body),
  which Slice 2 was about to clean.
- Both anchors disappeared in the same Slice 2 edit; the type was
  retired in the same slice rather than left as a future cleanup.

Same-name disambiguation check (mandatory before deletion): grep for
`class ChapterImage` and `data class ChapterImage` across the tree
to confirm no shadowing. Result: 3 distinct declarations exist (the
deleted one + 2 source-package-specific types `sources_repositry/ar/
mangamello/models/pages/ChapterImage.kt` and a `SwatChapterImage` in
`swatmanga`). The 2 surviving types are in different packages with
distinct call graphs and were NOT touched.

### Audit methodology cheatsheet update — discipline #16

Carrying forward §246 disciplines #1-#15. Adding discipline #16
discovered during Slice 2:

16. **Coupled-dead type retirement — drop the type along with its
    only anchor** — Slice 2's `chaptersImages` field drop also
    revealed `me.manga.kira.domain.model.ChapterImage` had zero
    remaining callers. The naive "field-prune only" scope would have
    left an orphan declaration. Instead, the type was deleted in the
    SAME slice. Discipline: for every field-prune of a typed field
    (i.e. the field's type is a project-defined ADT, not a stdlib
    primitive), grep `import <fqn-of-type>` AND `<typename>(`
    (constructor calls) across the entire `*.kt` tree AFTER the
    field drop. If both return 0, the type itself is coupled-dead
    and should be retired in the same slice. Mandatory same-name
    disambiguation: confirm the type is not shadowed by an
    identically-named declaration in another package — there may
    be multiple `Foo` declarations across the tree, and only the
    fully-qualified one matches the orphan call graph.

## Phase 9.y.coreplatform.modelsurvey.cumulative (Task #419) — :core + :platform model-layer survey (NULL RESULT)

### Slice intent

§247's next-candidate block advanced to entry (6) — the
`:core/.../model/*.kt` + `:platform/.../model/*.kt` model-layer
survey, mirroring §245's `:shared` methodology on the rework
modules. With §245-§247 having closed the `:shared` model-layer
field-prune campaign (118 symbols dropped + 1 coupled-dead type
retired), the question for this slice is: *do the rework `:core`
+ `:platform` modules have any orphan value-object declarations
or orphan fields that escaped the §245 sweep because they live
outside `:shared`?*

This entry documents the survey scope, per-declaration
verdicts, the null-result finding, and the
sealed-OCP-extension-reserve commentary that explains why
~12 orphan-looking AppError subclasses are correctly NOT pruned.

### Audit method

Same 3-pass receiver-anchored grep used in §245/§247:

| Pass | Pattern | Catches |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `\.X\(` / `\.field` | dotted-receiver access (most common) |
| 2 | `\bX\b` | bare-identifier references (rare for fields, common for type names in `when` arms) |
| 3 | `::X` | member references (rare for value-object members) |

For sealed types the audit ALSO checks parent-type consumers in
exhaustive `when (it)` blocks: a parent-level
`is AppError.Foo ->` arm catches every subclass uniformly, so
orphan-looking subclasses are LIVE-via-parent if any branch
consumes the parent type.

### Audit scope

The "model-layer" filter targets value-object-shaped declarations
(data class, sealed class, enum, top-level `const val`/`val`).
SPI facade interfaces (Logger, FeatureFlagProvider,
DispatcherProvider, all 24 `:platform` facades) are out-of-scope.

### Why this verdict is correct (defence-in-depth for AppError)

The ~12 AppError subclasses with zero `.kt` producers
(Network.Serialization, Storage.{NotFound, Constraint},
Validation.{Required, OutOfRange, Format}, Auth.{NotSignedIn,
Forbidden, TokenExpired}, Platform.{PermissionDenied,
FeatureUnavailable}, Cancelled) look like classic prune
candidates under a producer-only audit. They are NOT, for three
independent reasons:

1. **Class-level KDoc documents the design.** `AppError.kt:12-15`
   states verbatim: *"OCP: extending the hierarchy is allowed
   (sealed → callers must exhaustively handle new cases),
   modifying existing subclasses is not — adding behavior should
   produce a new subclass."* Pruning subclasses to "match current
   producers" violates this explicit OCP contract.

2. **Parent sealed types are LIVE.** The 3 `:ui` toUserMessage
   extensions (LibraryScreen.kt:1165, DetailsScreen.kt:512,
   ReaderScreen.kt:1141) all consume the parents via
   `is AppError.Network ->`, `is AppError.Storage ->`, etc. The
   Kotlin compiler treats those arms as exhaustive across the
   sealed parent — every existing AND future subclass is caught
   uniformly. Removing subclasses doesn't reduce the consumer
   surface; ADDING subclasses doesn't require updating consumers.

3. **Subclass field axes document the failure-mode design.**
   `Storage.NotFound(val key: String)`, `Validation.Required(val
   field: String)`, `Platform.PermissionDenied(val permission:
   String)` etc. each carry a named field that documents the
   diagnostic axis of that failure mode. Pruning them and
   re-introducing them later means redoing the design work and
   re-coordinating across `:data` mappers + telemetry pipelines.
   The current state is a feature, not a bug.

### Why this verdict differs from §247's coupled-dead retirement

§247 retired `ChapterImage` as coupled-dead because its only
field was orphan-pending-prune AND the class header had no
"reserve for future use" documentation. AppError subclasses have
the OPPOSITE documentation: an explicit OCP-extension-reserve
KDoc. Both verdicts follow from the SAME audit discipline
applied to DIFFERING class-header documentation — not from
inconsistent application of the discipline.

### Visibility narrowing alternative — rejected

Could the orphan subclasses be marked `internal` or hidden behind
factory fns? Rejected:

1. Internal sealed subclasses are valid Kotlin, but they would
   break the cross-module `is AppError.Network.Serialization ->`
   pattern that future producer slices need. The whole reason the
   subclasses are in `:core` is so `:data`/`:presentation`/`:ui`
   can all reference them.
2. Factory functions ("`AppError.notFound(key)`") would
   indirect away from the data-class destructuring pattern that
   pattern-matching `when` arms benefit from. The current
   construct-by-name pattern is more readable.
3. Adding `@PublishedApi` or `@Suppress` annotations to silence
   IDE "unused" warnings is gratuitous noise — the class-header
   KDoc already documents the design.

**Action: no source change.**

files) with a NEW corollary documented in ARCHITECTURE.md §248:

> **Discipline #17 — sealed-OCP-extension-reserve recognition.**
> Before declaring a sealed subclass orphan, read the class-level
> KDoc on the sealed root. If the root explicitly documents an
> OCP-extension-reserve posture, then orphan-looking subclasses
> are LIVE-via-OCP-reserve and MUST NOT be pruned. Verify the
> parent sealed type is consumed by at least one exhaustive
> `when` site (which keeps the whole hierarchy alive); if it is,
> the subclass is kept.

Discipline #17 is a refinement of #15: where #15 says "audit ALL
files," #17 says "audit the class-level KDoc TOO — it may
document a design intent that flips the prune verdict."

§248's next-candidate block advanced to entry (7) — the

This survey targets sealed-class subclass declarations and
enum-entry declarations whose runtime reachability depends on
per-call-site `when (...)` exhaustiveness rather than direct
producer/consumer reaches.

orphan — `shared/.../ad_mob/AdState.kt` — and the close-out

§371/§372 single-file precedent. The remaining sealed/enum
declarations across `:shared` fall into Tier-A LIVE (16 types),

COUPLED-DEAD (7 WhatsNew legacy files), each flagged for
separate dedicated slices.

### Audit method

Same 3-pass receiver-anchored grep as §245/§247/§248:

| Pass | Pattern | Catches |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | qualified-name (`AdState.Idle`, `Language.AR`, ...) | dotted-receiver / enum-entry references |
| 2 | bare-identifier (filtered for noise) | `import`-line + `when (it) -> is Foo ->` arms |
| 3 | `import.*<package>` | import-only usages + cross-validates the package reach surface |

Each subtype is LIVE if Pass 1 OR Pass 2 yields ≥1
runtime-reachable consumer (excluding `migration/` audit-doc
references).

### Audit discipline reinforced

This slice extends discipline #17 (sealed-OCP-extension-reserve
recognition) with a new corollary documented in ARCHITECTURE.md
§249:

> **Discipline #18 — sole-inhabitant package retire.**
> When the 3-pass grep confirms a sealed/enum declaration is a
> whole-file orphan AND that file is the sole inhabitant of
> its package directory, the retire MUST delete the directory
> alongside the file. Leaving an empty package directory is
> a maintenance footgun (future IDE navigation + future
> audits both waste cycles on empty dirs).

This slice retires the `ad_mob/` directory entirely by deleting
its sole inhabitant file.
